observations.title: Responsive mobile nav — MobileMenu drawer with full a11y
observations.content:
**What**: Made the global nav responsive. NavClient now renders desktop inline links (`hidden md:flex`) + a new `MobileMenu` (`md:hidden`) hamburger→drawer. Links are derived once from session (role-aware) and reused by both. SearchBox gained a `fullWidth` prop to live in the drawer.
**Why**: Audit found the navbar was a flat flex row with zero responsive classes — overflowed on ~360px. Content/pages were already responsive; only the nav wasn't. (CLAUDE.md/Pantallas falsely claimed a mobile menu existed.)
**Where**: components/layout/MobileMenu.tsx (new), components/layout/NavClient.tsx, components/buscar/SearchBox.tsx, promts/Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md
**Learned**: The project had NO drawer/modal primitive and NO icon library — icons are inline SVG (heroicons paths), reused that. The 3 existing ad-hoc modals lack focus-trap/scroll-lock/Escape/returnFocus; MobileMenu implements all of it properly and is the new reference for accessible overlays: `role="dialog" aria-modal`, document-level Escape, Tab-cycle focus trap, `document.body` scroll-lock, React 19 `inert` on the panel when closed (so off-screen links leave the tab order), returnFocus to the trigger, slide via `transition-transform` + `motion-reduce`. Future work: extract a shared Drawer/Modal primitive and retrofit the 3 modals. Hamburger is h-12 (48px, WCAG 2.5.5). Related: [[architecture/tailwind-v4-theme-vars]].

observations.title: sdd/es_vitrina/testing-capabilities
observations.content:
## Testing Capabilities

**Strict TDD Mode**: enabled (per CLAUDE.md/global agent marker), scope-limited to pure logic — see note below
**Detected**: 2026-07-10 (supersedes 2026-06-23 observation which predates vitest adoption)

### Test Runner

- Command: `pnpm test` (= `vitest run`)
- Framework: Vitest ^4.1.10
- Config: `vitest.config.ts` — environment `node`, include `**/*.test.ts`, exclude `node_modules`, `.next`, `testsprite_tests`

### Test Layers

| Layer       | Available | Tool                                                                 |
| ----------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Unit        | partial ✅ | Vitest — ONLY pure, side-effect-free logic (2 files today: `lib/supabase/handleError.test.ts`, `lib/storage/validateFile.test.ts`) |
| Integration | ❌ (via MCP) | `testsprite` MCP — API contracts, RLS/invariant checks |
| E2E         | ❌ (via MCP/skill) | `testsprite` MCP + `webapp-testing` skill (Playwright, needs `pnpm dev` running) |

### Coverage

- Available: ❌ (no `--coverage` flag wired into `pnpm test`)
- Command: —

### Quality Tools

| Tool         | Available | Command                    |
| ------------ | --------- | --------------------------- |
| Linter       | ✅        | `pnpm lint` (ESLint 9 flat config, `eslint.config.mjs`) |
| Type checker | ✅        | `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`   |
| Formatter    | ❌        | — (none configured)        |

### Strict TDD forwarding note (read before sdd-apply)

CLAUDE.md carries a global "Strict TDD Mode: enabled" marker, so per the decision gate (marker found → use that value) `strict_tdd` resolves to **true**. BUT the project's own Testing section explicitly scopes Vitest coverage to pure, side-effect-free logic only — it does **not** cover components, pages, or anything calling Supabase directly (`lib/data/*.ts`).

Practical forwarding rule for `sdd-apply`:
- New/changed pure functions (validators, mappers, `handleError`-style logic, pure `lib/*` helpers) → enforce red-green TDD with `pnpm test` (target the specific `*.test.ts` file, then full `pnpm test` before done).
- New/changed Server Components, Route Handlers, pages, or anything touching `lib/data/*.ts`/Supabase → no local unit-test gate exists; substitute verification is `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` + `pnpm lint`, plus `testsprite` MCP and/or `webapp-testing` (Playwright) for behavioral checks. Do not block on writing a Vitest test for these — there is no harness for them per project convention.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs lint, typecheck, test, and build as 4 independent parallel jobs on Node 22 — treat all four as the real merge gate, not just `pnpm test`.

**resolved test_command for strict-tdd forwarding**: `pnpm test` (vitest run), scope = pure logic under `lib/**` matching `**/*.test.ts` only.

observations.title: sdd/comentarios-hilos/explore
observations.content:
**What**: Exploration for "comentarios-hilos" — adding 2-level reply threads to publication comments.

**Why**: Tarea 1 from promts/promts/promt2.md. Feature adds threaded replies (max depth 2) to the existing flat comment system.

---

## Verified Starting Facts

### POST handler — app/api/comentarios/route.ts
- Destructures `{ publicacion_id, contenido }` from body — no `responde_a` yet.
- Gets user via `supabase.auth.getUser()`, returns `unauthorized()` if no user.
- Validates presence + `contenido.length <= 250`, inserts `{ publicacion_id, contenido, autor_id: user.id }`.
- Returns `jsonOk({ comentario: data }, 201)`.
- DELETE at `app/api/comentarios/[id]/route.ts` — only DELETE (204), RLS-enforced; uses Next 16 async `ctx.params`.

### DTO — lib/types/database.ts
- `Comentario = { id, contenido, publicacion_id, autor_id, creado_en, usuario?: Pick<Usuario,'id'|'nombre'> }`. No `responde_a` yet.
- `PublicacionDetalle.comentario` is `(Comentario & { usuario?... })[]` — flat array.

### Data layer
- `lib/data/publicaciones.ts` — `getPublicacion()` uses `.select('*, usuario(id, nombre), comentario(*, usuario(id, nombre)), publicacion_tag(*, tag(*))')` with `.single()`. No explicit order on embedded `comentario`.
- `lib/data/comentarios.ts` — `getComentarios(publicacionId)` selects `*, usuario(id, nombre)` ordered by `creado_en desc`. Used ONLY by the GET route handler, NOT by the detail page.

### Components
- `ComentarioList.tsx` — Server Component, flat `<ul>`, prop `comentarios: (Comentario & { usuario?... })[]`.
- `ComentarioForm.tsx` — 'use client', prop `publicacionId: string`, no `responde_a`. POSTs `{ publicacion_id, contenido }`, on success calls `router.refresh()`.
- Field component: `multiline` prop renders `<textarea>`, handles `onChange` for both input and textarea.

### Detail page — app/(main)/publicacion/[id]/page.tsx
- Uses Next 16 async `params`: `const { id } = await params`.
- Calls `getPublicacion(id)`, then extracts `const comentarios = (data.comentario ?? [])`.
- Passes `isAuthenticated = Boolean(user)` to render logic.
- Renders `<ComentarioList comentarios={comentarios} />` and conditionally `<ComentarioForm publicacionId={id} />` (when `isAuthenticated`).
- Anonymous users see a "Iniciá sesión para comentar" link instead.

### supabase-js ordering capability
- `lib/data/revistas.ts` uses `.order('orden', { referencedTable: 'revista_articulo', ascending: true })` on an embedded relation — confirms referencedTable ordering works for embedded embeds.
- However: comments will be fetched flat (ALL comments for publication in one query) and sorted in memory, so embedded ordering in `getPublicacion` is NOT the right approach.

---

## Analysis by Question

### Q1: Single-query tree load — extend getPublicacion vs dedicated getComentariosArbol

**Option A**: Add ordering inside `getPublicacion` embedded select.
- Problem: supabase-js `referencedTable` ordering applies to a flat embedded result. It cannot express "roots desc, replies within thread asc" in one embedded query. The embedded `comentario(*)` in getPublicacion returns a flat array with no order guarantee between roots vs replies.
- `getPublicacion` already does many joins (usuario, comentario, publicacion_tag). Adding more complexity here violates single-responsibility and makes the function harder to test.

**Option B**: Dedicated `getComentariosArbol(publicacionId)` in `lib/data/comentarios.ts`.
- ONE flat query: `select('*, usuario(id, nombre)').eq('publicacion_id', id).order('creado_en', { ascending: true })`. Fetch ALL comments for the publication in ascending order.
- Build the 2-level tree IN MEMORY: group by `responde_a IS NULL` for roots, then attach replies to their root.
- Apply ordering in memory: roots sorted by `creado_en desc` (reverse the flat array or sort after grouping); replies within each thread already in `creado_en asc` (natural from the query order).
- The detail page calls `getComentariosArbol` separately from `getPublicacion`. This avoids the embedded-sort impossibility.
- RECOMMENDATION: **Option B**. Keep `getPublicacion` unchanged; add `getComentariosArbol` to `lib/data/comentarios.ts`; update the detail page to call both in `Promise.all` to avoid a waterfall.

**Change to detail page**: Replace `data.comentario` extraction with the result of `getComentariosArbol(id)`. Call it in parallel with other independent data fetches (likes, guardados, etc.) via `Promise.all`.

### Q2: Same-publication validation + re-parent-to-root in POST — minimum queries

The algorithm needs to:
1. Validate `responde_a` references an existing comment.
2. Validate that comment belongs to the SAME `publicacion_id`.
3. Determine if that comment is itself a reply (has its own `responde_a`) and if so, re-parent to the root.

**Minimum approach — ONE select**:
```
select id, publicacion_id, responde_a
from comentario
where id = :responde_a_from_body
```
Returns: `{ id, publicacion_id, responde_a }`.
- If no row → 400 (comment not found).
- If `row.publicacion_id !== body.publicacion_id` → 400 (cross-publication).
- If `row.responde_a !== null` → re-parent: use `row.responde_a` as the actual `responde_a` to insert (re-parent to root).
- If `row.responde_a === null` → it's a root, use `row.id` directly.

This is exactly ONE extra query before the insert. Since re-parenting goes one level (the referenced comment's own `responde_a` is already the root because we enforce max-depth-2 at insert time), chasing one level is sufficient.

**Edge case**: What if someone bypasses the API and inserts a depth-3 comment directly to the DB? The POST logic, re-parenting by checking one level, would re-anchor to the intermediate node which itself should be anchored to root. In practice: since all inserts go through this handler, the invariant holds. No need for recursive resolution.

### Q3: In-memory tree shape and markup

Proposed type to expose to ComentarioList:

```typescript
export type ComentarioConUsuario = Comentario & {
  usuario?: Pick<Usuario, 'id' | 'nombre'> | null
}

export type ComentarioArbol = ComentarioConUsuario & {
  responde_a: string | null
  respuestas: ComentarioConUsuario[]
}
```

Tree-building in lib/data/comentarios.ts (in memory):
1. Fetch all flat, `creado_en asc`.
2. Separate roots (`responde_a === null`) and replies.
3. Build a Map<rootId, replies[]> for O(1) lookup.
4. Sort roots `creado_en desc` (reverse); replies within each root stay `creado_en asc`.

Markup approach:
- ComentarioList receives `comentarios: ComentarioArbol[]` (roots only).
- `<ul>` for roots; inside each `<li>`, if `comentario.respuestas.length > 0`, render a `<ul class="ml-6 mt-3 flex flex-col gap-3">` (indented) with the replies — simple, no recursion, hardcoded 2 levels.
- "Responder" button goes inside each root `<li>`, only when `isAuthenticated` prop is true.
- The inline reply form mounts inside the root `<li>` conditionally when that root is the "active reply target".

ComentarioList must become a Client Component (needs `useState` for the active reply target). This is the ONLY component that changes its RSC boundary — currently it's a Server Component.

### Q4: ComentarioForm — respondaA prop + inline toggle

ComentarioForm gets two new optional props:
- `respondaA?: string | null` — if set, the form sends `responde_a` in the POST body.
- `onSuccess?: () => void` — callback for inline reply forms (to collapse the form after submit).

The "Responder" toggle lives in ComentarioList (now a Client Component):
- `const [replyingTo, setReplyingTo] = useState<string | null>(null)`.
- Per root comment: if `replyingTo === comentario.id` → render `<ComentarioForm publicacionId={...} respondaA={comentario.id} onSuccess={() => setReplyingTo(null)} />` inline below the comment body.
- "Responder" button: `onClick={() => setReplyingTo(id)}`. If already open: toggles closed (`onClick={() => setReplyingTo(replyingTo === id ? null : id)`).
- On success: `onSuccess()` collapses the form AND calls `router.refresh()` (must move `useRouter` call to ComentarioList since it now owns the refresh).

ComentarioForm changes:
- Add `respondaA?: string | null` prop.
- Add `onSuccess?: () => void` prop — called after successful submit (before or after `router.refresh()`).
- POST body includes `responde_a: respondaA` when set.
- When `respondaA` is set: label changes to "Tu respuesta", placeholder to "Escribí tu respuesta…".

The main (root-level) ComentarioForm in page.tsx remains with no `respondaA`. It already calls `router.refresh()` on success.

### Q5: Anonymous vs authenticated rendering

The page already computes `isAuthenticated`. Pass it as a prop to ComentarioList:

```
<ComentarioList comentarios={comentariosArbol} isAuthenticated={isAuthenticated} />
```

- `isAuthenticated = false` → no "Responder" buttons anywhere; threads visible read-only. The existing anonymous "Iniciá sesión para comentar" message stays below the list.
- `isAuthenticated = true` → "Responder" buttons on root comments only (not on replies, since replies can't be replied to at depth 2).

### Q6: Edge cases and gotchas

**Cascade delete**: `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `responde_a` references `comentario(id)`. This means deleting a root comment cascades to its replies. This is intentional (promt2.md says so). The existing DELETE handler at `[id]/route.ts` handles this — RLS lets the author delete their own comment, and the cascade handles children at DB level.

**Reply-to-reply re-parenting**: Handled in POST with one select (see Q2). The invariant is maintained at insert time, so the DB never has depth > 2 via the API.

**Validation error codes**: All validation in the POST must use `validationError(message)` (→ 400 with `code: 'validation_error'`). The "comment not found" case is also a 400 validation_error (not a 404, since the endpoint contract is comment creation, not comment lookup). Cross-publication is a 400 validation_error.

**`like` reserved word note**: Irrelevant for comentario — the table name `comentario` is not a reserved SQL word. No quoting needed. No change here.

**Next 16 async params**: The DELETE handler at `[id]/route.ts` already uses `const { id } = await ctx.params` (correct Next 16 pattern). The POST handler and GET handler don't use params — no change needed.

**supabase-js ordering in embedded comentario inside getPublicacion**: The current `getPublicacion` embed doesn't order comments. After this change, `getPublicacion` should NOT be used for comments — the detail page will call `getComentariosArbol` separately. The `PublicacionDetalle.comentario` field becomes unused at the page level (but the DTO can keep it for backward compatibility with other potential callers).

**The `getComentarios` function (GET route)**: This returns a flat list for the GET route handler. It can stay as-is (flat, ordered by `creado_en desc`). The GET route is a client-facing endpoint; if callers need the threaded view they should use the detail page. Alternatively, the GET route could also return the tree — but the spec says only edit the POST handler; the GET route is not mentioned. Keep it flat for now.

**`comentarios.length` count in the page heading**: Currently `{comentarios.length}` shows total flat count. After this change, `comentariosArbol` is an array of roots. The count should reflect ALL comments (roots + replies). The page should compute total from the flat fetch, or expose a totalCount alongside the tree.

**ComentarioList RSC boundary change**: This is the only boundary change. ComentarioList must become `'use client'` because it needs `useState` for the reply toggle. This is appropriate — it's a leaf component, not a layout or page.

### Q7: Docs to update in promts/

**Vitrina_BD_Conexion_Backend.md**:
- §comentario table schema row: add `responde_a uuid? FK → comentario(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`.
- Add a note under the aditivas exceptions documenting `comentarios_hilos` migration.
- Update cascade note: deleting a comment also cascades its replies (via self-referential FK).

**Vitrina_Especificaciones_APIs.md**:
- §4.4 `comentario` POST: update payload to include optional `responde_a?: uuid`. Add validation rules: existence check, same-publication check, re-parenting logic.
- §8 DTO table: update `comentario` row to include `responde_a uuid?`.

**Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md**:
- §3.2 ComentarioList: update description from "flat list" to "2-level thread list"; add `isAuthenticated` prop; note "Responder" buttons on root comments only.
- §3.2 ComentarioForm: add `respondaA?` and `onSuccess?` props; note inline reply usage.
- Component tree in §3.2: ComentarioList now 'use client'.

---

## Approach Comparison Table

| Fork | Option A: extend getPublicacion embed | Option B: dedicated getComentariosArbol (RECOMMENDED) |
|------|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Single query | Yes, but ordering roots-desc/replies-asc impossible in one embedded query | Yes — flat query, in-memory sort |
| Coupling | High — getPublicacion already does 3 joins; harder to test | Low — isolated function |
| Page waterfall | None (same query) | Minor: must use Promise.all with other fetches |
| Flexibility | Hard to evolve (nested select limitations) | Easy to extend (e.g., paginate, filter) |
| Code clarity | Poor — sort logic hidden in data layer mixed with other joins | Clean — separate concern |

| Fork | ComentarioList stays Server Component | ComentarioList becomes Client Component (RECOMMENDED) |
|------|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Reply toggle | Not possible (no useState) | Natural (useState for replyingTo) |
| Bundle impact | None added | Adds ComentarioList to client bundle |
| Alternative | Separate ReplyButton client island + server ComentarioList | Simpler, less fragmentation |
| Recommendation | Only viable if we use a separate client island per comment | Preferred — ComentarioList is already a leaf |

---

## Recommended Approach Summary

1. **Migration**: `alter table comentario add column responde_a uuid references comentario(id) on delete cascade` — via Supabase MCP on project fdfbyhjwnbteccagulxb.
2. **DTO**: Add `responde_a: string | null` to `Comentario`; add `ComentarioArbol` type with `respuestas: ComentarioConUsuario[]`.
3. **Data layer**: Add `getComentariosArbol(publicacionId)` to `lib/data/comentarios.ts` — ONE flat query, in-memory tree build.
4. **Detail page**: Call `getComentariosArbol` in parallel with `getLikesInfo` etc. via `Promise.all`; pass result to `<ComentarioList>` with `isAuthenticated`.
5. **POST handler**: Accept optional `responde_a`; if present, one select to validate existence + same publication + re-parent if needed.
6. **ComentarioList**: Convert to `'use client'`; add `isAuthenticated` prop + `replyingTo` state; render inline `ComentarioForm` per root when active.
7. **ComentarioForm**: Add `respondaA?` and `onSuccess?` props; include in POST body when set.
8. **Docs**: Update BD §comentario, APIs §4.4 + §8 DTO, Pantallas §3.2.

**Where**: app/api/comentarios/route.ts, lib/types/database.ts, lib/data/comentarios.ts, lib/data/publicaciones.ts (detail page), app/(main)/publicacion/[id]/page.tsx, components/publicacion/ComentarioList.tsx, components/publicacion/ComentarioForm.tsx, promts/*.md.

observations.title: sdd/comentarios-hilos/proposal
observations.content:
## Proposal — comentarios-hilos (Tarea 1: 2-level reply threads)

### Intent (why)
**Problem**: The publication detail page (`app/(main)/publicacion/[id]/page.tsx`) renders comments as a single flat list. Users cannot reply to a specific comment — every comment is a top-level remark, so conversations have no structure and follow-ups are impossible to follow.

**Why now**: Tarea 1 from `promts/promts/promt2.md` mandates threaded replies with a maximum depth of 2 (root comment + one level of replies). This is the next committed MVP feature for the comment system.

**Success looks like**:
- A signed-in user can reply to any root comment via an inline "Responder" form; the reply renders indented under that root.
- Replies to a reply re-anchor to the root (the tree never exceeds depth 2), regardless of which comment the user clicked.
- Anonymous visitors can READ full threads but see no "Responder" button.
- Deleting a root comment removes its replies automatically (DB cascade).
- The response envelope, RLS/RPC invariants, and `promts/` docs stay correct and in sync.

### Scope

**In scope**
- Additive migration `comentarios_hilos`: `alter table comentario add column responde_a uuid references comentario(id) on delete cascade` (nullable). Applied via Supabase MCP (project ref `fdfbyhjwnbteccagulxb`), then committed to a migration file.
- DTO updates in `lib/types/database.ts`: add `responde_a: string | null` to `Comentario`; add `ComentarioConUsuario` and `ComentarioArbol` (`{ ...comentario, respuestas: ComentarioConUsuario[] }`) types.
- New data-layer function `getComentariosArbol(publicacionId)` in `lib/data/comentarios.ts` — one flat query + in-memory 2-level tree build. Returns roots plus a separately-computed total count.
- POST handler `app/api/comentarios/route.ts`: accept optional `responde_a`; one pre-insert select to validate existence + same-publication + re-parent reply-to-reply to root.
- `ComentarioList.tsx`: convert to Client Component; add `isAuthenticated` prop + `replyingTo` state + inline reply form per root; render 2-level markup.
- `ComentarioForm.tsx`: add optional `respondaA?: string | null` and `onSuccess?: () => void` props.
- Detail page `app/(main)/publicacion/[id]/page.tsx`: call `getComentariosArbol(id)` (in parallel via `Promise.all` with other independent fetches), pass tree + `isAuthenticated` + total count to `ComentarioList`.
- Docs sync: `Vitrina_BD_Conexion_Backend.md` (schema + cascade + aditiva note), `Vitrina_Especificaciones_APIs.md` (§4.4 POST payload/validation + §8 DTO), `Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md` (§3.2 ComentarioList/ComentarioForm).

**Out of scope**
- Any change to RLS, RPC, views (`feed_publicaciones`), triggers, or existing policies — strictly forbidden.
- `service_role` / `admin.ts` — CERO. User JWT only.
- Editing comments, reply-to-reply UI affordances (replies show no "Responder" button), notifications, pagination of comments, optimistic UI.
- The GET route `getComentarios` (flat, `creado_en desc`) and the DELETE handler `[id]/route.ts` — left untouched (cascade is handled at DB level by the FK; the spec only calls for editing the POST handler).
- `getPublicacion` embedded `comentario(*)` select — left as-is for backward compatibility; the detail page simply stops relying on it for comments.

### Approach (high level + rationale)
1. **Dedicated `getComentariosArbol` over extending `getPublicacion`** — supabase-js `referencedTable` ordering cannot express "roots desc + replies asc" in one embedded query, and `getPublicacion` already carries 3 joins. A dedicated function does ONE flat query (`select *, usuario(id, nombre) eq publicacion_id order creado_en asc`) and builds the tree in memory: group roots (`responde_a === null`) and replies, attach replies to roots via a `Map<rootId, replies[]>`, sort roots `creado_en desc`, keep replies `creado_en asc`. Isolated, testable, low coupling. Detail page calls it in parallel via `Promise.all` to avoid a waterfall.
2. **POST validation + re-parent in ONE select** — when `responde_a` is present, `select id, publicacion_id, responde_a from comentario where id = :responde_a`. No row → 400; `publicacion_id` mismatch → 400; if the target itself has `responde_a` (it's a reply) use its `responde_a` as the actual parent (re-anchor to root); otherwise use the target id. One level of chasing suffices because the API enforces the depth-2 invariant on every insert. `autor_id` always from `supabase.auth.getUser()`, never the body.
3. **ComentarioList becomes the only RSC-boundary change** — it needs `useState` for the active reply target and owns `useRouter().refresh()` after a successful reply. It is a leaf component, so the client-bundle cost is acceptable; the alternative (a separate per-comment client island) fragments the code more for no gain.
4. **ComentarioForm stays the shared form** — reused both as the root form (no `respondaA`) and the inline reply form (`respondaA` set, `onSuccess` collapses it). When `respondaA` is set, label/placeholder switch to reply copy and the POST body includes `responde_a`.
5. **Anonymous read-only** — page already computes `isAuthenticated`; passed to `ComentarioList`. False → threads render, no "Responder" buttons; existing "Iniciá sesión para comentar" link stays.

### Decided resolution — comment-count heading
The page heading currently shows `{comentarios.length}`, which was the flat total. After this change `comentariosArbol` is an array of ROOTS only, so its `.length` would undercount (it would exclude replies). **Decision**: compute the total = roots + replies SEPARATELY from the flat fetch, inside `getComentariosArbol`, and return it alongside the tree (e.g. `{ arbol, total }` where `total` is the length of the flat result before grouping). The page binds the heading to `total`, not to `arbol.length`. This keeps the displayed count truthful (all comments, roots and replies) without a second query.

### Affected files
- `supabase` migration `comentarios_hilos` (additive column)
- `lib/types/database.ts`
- `lib/data/comentarios.ts`
- `app/api/comentarios/route.ts`
- `components/publicacion/ComentarioList.tsx`
- `components/publicacion/ComentarioForm.tsx`
- `app/(main)/publicacion/[id]/page.tsx`
- `promts/Vitrina_BD_Conexion_Backend.md`, `promts/Vitrina_Especificaciones_APIs.md`, `promts/Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md`

### Risks / open questions
- **Depth-3 from out-of-band inserts**: re-parenting chases only one level. If a depth-3 row were inserted directly to the DB (bypassing the API), the in-memory tree would attach an orphaned reply to a non-root. Acceptable: all inserts go through the API which enforces depth 2. Documented, not mitigated.
- **`Promise.all` shape change in the page**: must confirm the existing parallel fetch block (likes/guardados/etc.) so `getComentariosArbol` is added without introducing a waterfall or breaking existing destructuring.
- **RSC→client boundary for `ComentarioList`**: verify no Server-only imports leak into it once it becomes `'use client'`.
- **Error-code contract**: "comment not found" and "cross-publication" are 400 `validation_error` (creation contract, not lookup) — must use the existing `validationError()` helper, not a 404.
- **Migration commit hygiene**: schema change via `execute_sql` (MCP) for iteration, then `supabase db pull comentarios_hilos --local` to capture the migration file; run `get_advisors` after.

### Verification criteria (from spec)
1. **Reply-to-reply anchors to root**: replying to a reply produces a comment whose stored `responde_a` is the ROOT id; the tree stays at depth 2.
2. **Cascade delete**: deleting a root comment removes all its replies (FK `on delete cascade`), verified via the existing DELETE handler under the author's JWT.
3. **Cross-publication `responde_a` → 400**: POST with a `responde_a` belonging to a different publication returns 400 `validation_error`.
4. **Anonymous read-only**: an anonymous visitor sees full threads but no "Responder" button; the "Iniciá sesión para comentar" prompt remains.

**Learned**: The single biggest design lever is using a dedicated flat-fetch + in-memory tree instead of embedded-relation ordering; supabase-js cannot order roots-desc/replies-asc in one nested select. The count heading is the easy-to-miss correctness bug — must derive total from the flat result, not from the roots array.

observations.title: sdd/comentarios-hilos/spec
observations.content:
# Spec — comentarios-hilos (2-level reply threads)

## 1. Scope

Delta spec: what MUST be true after the `comentarios-hilos` change is applied.
Baseline behaviour already passing (root comments, flat list, authenticated POST, DELETE, RLS) is not re-stated unless it is modified or must be explicitly preserved.

---

## 2. Data contracts

### 2.1 Comentario DTO (lib/types/database.ts)

```ts
interface Comentario {
  id: string                   // uuid
  publicacion_id: string       // uuid — FK publicacion.id
  autor_id: string             // uuid — FK usuario.id (auth.uid() at insert time)
  contenido: string
  creado_en: string            // ISO timestamp
  responde_a: string | null    // uuid — FK comentario.id (nullable; null = root comment)
}
```

`responde_a` is ADDITIVE: existing rows have `null`. The DB column has `ON DELETE CASCADE` so deleting a root removes all rows where `responde_a = root.id`.

### 2.2 ComentarioConUsuario DTO

```ts
interface ComentarioConUsuario extends Comentario {
  usuario: {
    id: string
    nombre: string
  }
}
```

### 2.3 ComentarioArbol shape

```ts
interface ComentarioArbol extends ComentarioConUsuario {
  respuestas: ComentarioConUsuario[]   // always present, possibly empty
}
```

### 2.4 getComentariosArbol return shape

```ts
{
  arbol: ComentarioArbol[]   // roots only, ordered creado_en DESC
  total: number              // roots + all replies (flat count before grouping)
}
```

---

## 3. Schema delta

### 3.1 Migration (additive, no RLS change)

```sql
ALTER TABLE comentario
  ADD COLUMN responde_a uuid
  REFERENCES comentario(id)
  ON DELETE CASCADE;
```

- Column is nullable; default null.
- All existing rows receive `responde_a = null` (unchanged semantics).
- No new RLS policy, no existing policy change, no new RPC, no view change.

---

## 4. API contract delta — POST /api/comentarios

### 4.1 Request body

```ts
{
  publicacion_id: string        // required
  contenido: string             // required, non-empty
  responde_a?: string | null    // optional — uuid of the target comment
}
```

`autor_id` is NEVER accepted in the body; it is ALWAYS derived from `supabase.auth.getUser()`.

### 4.2 Response

| Condition | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|
| Success (root or reply) | 201 | `{ data: Comentario }` |
| Unauthenticated / session invalid | 401 | `{ error: { code: "unauthorized", message: "..." } }` |
| `responde_a` not found | 400 | `{ error: { code: "validation_error", message: "..." } }` |
| `responde_a` belongs to different publicacion | 400 | `{ error: { code: "validation_error", message: "..." } }` |
| `publicacion_id` or `contenido` missing/empty | 400 | `{ error: { code: "validation_error", message: "..." } }` |
| DB unique / RLS denial | 409 / 403 | (existing handleError mapping, unchanged) |

### 4.3 Re-parent logic (server-side invariant)

When `responde_a` is present:

1. SELECT `id, publicacion_id, responde_a` FROM `comentario` WHERE `id = :responde_a`.
2. If no row → 400 validation_error.
3. If `publicacion_id` of target ≠ request `publicacion_id` → 400 validation_error.
4. If target's own `responde_a` IS NOT NULL (target is itself a reply) → use target's `responde_a` as the effective parent (re-anchor to root).
5. Otherwise use target's `id` as the effective parent.
6. Insert with effective parent; stored `responde_a` in the new row is always the root comment's `id` (depth ≤ 2 guaranteed).

---

## 5. Data-layer function

### 5.1 getComentariosArbol(publicacionId: string)

- ONE query: select all `comentario` rows for `publicacion_id` with joined `usuario(id, nombre)`, ordered `creado_en ASC` (replies ascending is sufficient; roots are reordered in memory).
- In-memory build:
  - Separate rows into roots (`responde_a === null`) and replies (`responde_a !== null`).
  - `total = rows.length` (captured before grouping).
  - Index replies by `responde_a` in a `Map<rootId, ComentarioConUsuario[]>`.
  - Attach replies array to each root; sort roots `creado_en DESC`.
- Return `{ arbol, total }`.
- Lives in `lib/data/comentarios.ts` (Server-only file).
- Called from the detail page inside `Promise.all` to avoid waterfall with existing parallel fetches (likes, guardados, etc.).

---

## 6. UI requirements

### 6.1 Comment count heading

- The page heading MUST bind to `total` (from `getComentariosArbol`), NOT to `arbol.length`.
- `total` counts roots + replies; `arbol.length` counts roots only and would undercount once replies exist.

### 6.2 Render order

- Root comments: `creado_en DESC` (newest first).
- Replies within a root thread: `creado_en ASC` (oldest first, conversation order).

### 6.3 Anonymous user

- Full thread (roots + replies) rendered.
- No "Responder" button anywhere in the tree.
- Existing "Iniciá sesión para comentar" prompt preserved in place of the root form.

### 6.4 Authenticated user

- "Responder" button visible ONLY on ROOT comments (not on replies — depth-2 cap enforced at UI level too).
- Clicking "Responder" shows an inline form directly under that root; clicking it again (or after success) collapses it.
- Only one reply form open at a time (controlled by a single `replyingTo: string | null` state in `ComentarioList`).

### 6.5 ComentarioList client boundary

- `ComentarioList` MUST be a Client Component (`'use client'`).
- After a reply is posted successfully, calls `useRouter().refresh()` to re-fetch the tree from the server.
- No Server-only imports (`lib/data/*`, `lib/supabase/server.ts`) must remain in this file after conversion.

### 6.6 ComentarioForm reuse

- `ComentarioForm` accepts optional `respondaA?: string | null` and `onSuccess?: () => void` props.
- When `respondaA` is set: POST body includes `responde_a`; form label/placeholder switches to reply copy; `onSuccess` is called on success (to collapse the inline form).
- When `respondaA` is absent (root form): behaviour unchanged from baseline.

---

## 7. Cascade delete

- Deleting a root comment (via existing DELETE handler under the comment owner's JWT) MUST remove all its replies automatically via the DB `ON DELETE CASCADE` FK.
- No application-level code handles reply deletion; the cascade is the only mechanism.
- The DELETE handler itself is NOT modified by this change.

---

## 8. Acceptance scenarios

### S-01 — Root comment (baseline preserved)

**Given** an authenticated user on a publication detail page  
**When** they submit a comment with `{ publicacion_id, contenido }` and no `responde_a`  
**Then** the API responds 201 with `{ data: Comentario }` where `responde_a` is `null`; the new comment appears at the TOP of the list (creado_en DESC ordering).

---

### S-02 — Reply to a root comment

**Given** an authenticated user  
**And** a root comment `C1` belonging to `publicacion_id = P1`  
**When** they POST `{ publicacion_id: "P1", contenido: "...", responde_a: "C1" }`  
**Then** the API responds 201; the stored row has `responde_a = C1.id`; the reply renders indented under `C1` in the UI (not as a new root).

---

### S-03 — Reply to a reply → re-parented to root

**Given** a root comment `C1` and a reply `C2` where `C2.responde_a = C1.id`  
**When** a user POSTs `{ publicacion_id: P1, contenido: "...", responde_a: "C2" }`  
**Then** the API detects that `C2.responde_a` is not null → re-parents to `C1.id`; the stored row has `responde_a = C1.id`; the tree depth stays at 2; the response is 201.

---

### S-04 — Cross-publication responde_a → 400

**Given** comment `C_other` belongs to `publicacion_id = P2`  
**When** a user POSTs `{ publicacion_id: "P1", contenido: "...", responde_a: "C_other.id" }`  
**Then** the API responds 400 with `{ error: { code: "validation_error", message: "..." } }`; no row is inserted.

---

### S-05 — Non-existent responde_a → 400

**Given** a UUID that does not match any row in `comentario`  
**When** a user POSTs `{ publicacion_id: "P1", contenido: "...", responde_a: "<ghost-uuid>" }`  
**Then** the API responds 400 with `{ error: { code: "validation_error", message: "..." } }`; no row is inserted.

---

### S-06 — Unauthenticated POST → 401

**Given** no valid session cookie (anonymous or expired)  
**When** any POST to `/api/comentarios` is made  
**Then** the API responds 401; `autor_id` is never derived from body; no row is inserted.

---

### S-07 — autor_id from session only

**Given** an authenticated user `U1` posts with a body that includes `autor_id: "U2-uuid"`  
**Then** the stored row has `autor_id = U1.auth.uid()` (the session user), not `U2-uuid`; the injected field is silently ignored.

---

### S-08 — Comment count heading (total, not roots only)

**Given** a publication with 3 root comments and 4 replies (total 7)  
**When** the detail page renders  
**Then** the heading shows "7 comentarios" (not "3 comentarios"); `total` from `getComentariosArbol` is used.

---

### S-09 — Render order

**Given** a publication with roots `C1` (oldest) and `C2` (newest), and replies `R1` (older) and `R2` (newer) under `C1`  
**When** the detail page renders  
**Then** `C2` appears ABOVE `C1` (roots DESC); within `C1`'s thread `R1` appears ABOVE `R2` (replies ASC).

---

### S-10 — Anonymous read-only

**Given** an anonymous visitor (no session)  
**When** they view a publication with threaded comments  
**Then** all roots and replies are visible; no "Responder" button is rendered anywhere; the "Iniciá sesión para comentar" prompt is visible in place of the root form.

---

### S-11 — Authenticated: Responder only on roots

**Given** an authenticated user  
**When** they view a publication with a root comment `C1` and its reply `R1`  
**Then** a "Responder" button appears next to `C1`; NO "Responder" button appears next to `R1`.

---

### S-12 — Inline reply form toggle

**Given** an authenticated user views a root comment `C1`  
**When** they click "Responder" on `C1`  
**Then** an inline reply form appears under `C1`; clicking "Responder" again (or a different root's "Responder") collapses the previous form; only one reply form is open at a time.

---

### S-13 — Cascade delete

**Given** a root comment `C1` with replies `R1` and `R2` (`responde_a = C1.id`)  
**When** the author (or admin, per existing policy) DELETEs `C1` via the existing DELETE handler  
**Then** `R1` and `R2` are also removed from the DB (FK ON DELETE CASCADE); the detail page re-renders showing 0 comments for that thread; no application-level code deletes the replies explicitly.

---

## 9. Out-of-scope invariants (must NOT change)

- RLS policies — zero modifications.
- RPC `aceptar_solicitud` / `rechazar_solicitud` — untouched.
- View `feed_publicaciones` — untouched.
- `service_role` usage — remains ZERO.
- Existing DELETE handler `app/api/comentarios/[id]/route.ts` — not modified.
- Flat GET handler `app/api/comentarios/route.ts` GET path — not modified.
- `getPublicacion` embedded `comentario(*)` select — not modified (detail page stops relying on it for comments, but the select itself stays).
- Pagination, optimistic UI, comment editing, notifications — out of scope.

---

## 10. Docs sync (mandatory alongside code changes)

| Document | What to update |
|---|---|
| `promts/Vitrina_BD_Conexion_Backend.md` | Schema exception note: additive `responde_a` column, FK, cascade; no RLS change |
| `promts/Vitrina_Especificaciones_APIs.md` | §4.4 POST body adds optional `responde_a`; validation rules; 400 cases; DTO §8 adds `responde_a`, `ComentarioArbol` |
| `promts/Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md` | §3.2 `ComentarioList` (client component, props, reply toggle), `ComentarioForm` (new props), detail page heading bound to `total` |

observations.title: sdd/es_vitrina/comentarios-hilos/design
observations.content:
# Design — comentarios-hilos (2-level reply threads)

Architectural HOW for the proposal (#129). Reads proposal + exploration + current source (verified 2026-06-23). This is design-level (boundaries, data flow, contracts), NOT task steps.

## Chosen architecture (pattern + rationale)
- **Self-referential FK on `comentario` + API-enforced depth-2 invariant + in-memory tree build in the data layer.** Depth is NOT enforced by a DB constraint (Postgres can't cheaply express "parent must be a root" without a trigger, and triggers are out of scope / forbidden touching). The POST handler is the single write path and is the sole enforcer of the depth-2 invariant via re-parenting. The DB stores a flat adjacency list; the read side reconstructs a 2-level tree in memory.
- **Layering preserved (Screaming/Clean-ish split already in the repo):** Route Handler = mutation + validation; `lib/data/*` = SERVER-ONLY reads (SSR); Server Component page = orchestration; Client Component = interactivity only. The ONLY RSC→client boundary that moves is `ComentarioList` (gains `useState`).
- **No new module/folder.** All changes land in existing files. No new abstraction layer; a single new exported function + two new DTO types.

## Component & data-flow map
```
[DB] comentario(+responde_a FK self, on delete cascade)
   │  (flat read, creado_en asc)            │  (write: POST /api/comentarios)
   ▼                                         ▲
lib/data/comentarios.ts                      app/api/comentarios/route.ts (POST)
  getComentariosArbol(pubId)                   - autor_id from session
   → { arbol: ComentarioArbol[], total }       - optional responde_a → 1 pre-insert SELECT
   (flat query + in-memory grouping)           - re-parent reply→root, validate same-pub
   ▼                                            - insert effective responde_a
app/(main)/publicacion/[id]/page.tsx (RSC)    ▲
  - Promise.all(getComentariosArbol, …)        │ apiClient POST { publicacion_id, contenido, responde_a? }
  - passes { arbol, total, isAuthenticated }   │
   ▼                                      ComentarioForm ('use client') ── reused root + inline reply
ComentarioList ('use client')  ──────────────┘
  - replyingTo state, depth-2 markup, owns router.refresh()
```

Data flow:
1. **Read (SSR):** page → `getComentariosArbol(id)` (parallel with likes/guardados/etc.) → one flat supabase-js query → group in memory → `{ arbol, total }` → props to `ComentarioList`; `total` drives the heading count.
2. **Write (client):** user clicks "Responder" → `ComentarioList` sets `replyingTo` → inline `ComentarioForm` with `respondaA` → `apiClient` POST → handler validates/re-parents/inserts → `onSuccess` collapses form → `router.refresh()` re-runs the RSC read.

## ADR-1 — Self-referential FK, no DB-level depth constraint
**Decision:** `alter table comentario add column responde_a uuid references comentario(id) on delete cascade` (nullable). Additive only. Applied via Supabase MCP.
**Rationale:** Cascade delete of replies is a hard requirement (Tarea 1). FK gives referential integrity + cascade for free. Depth-2 is a domain rule the API owns, not the DB.
**Rejected:**
- *CHECK / trigger enforcing parent-is-root* — touches DB logic, harder to reason about, and triggers/RPC changes are forbidden by invariants. The API is already the single write path.
- *Separate `respuesta` table* — duplicates schema, breaks the existing flat DELETE/cascade story, more joins. No benefit at depth 2.
**Migration MCP workflow (per supabase skill):**
1. Iterate with `execute_sql` (MCP) until correct — does NOT write migration history, so you can re-run.
2. Verify shape with a `select` against `comentario`.
3. When correct: capture migration file via `supabase db pull comentarios_hilos --local --yes` (NOT `apply_migration`, which writes history on every call and breaks `db diff`). If pull is unavailable in this env, `apply_migration` ONCE with the final SQL is the fallback.
4. `get_advisors` (security + performance) after; fix anything raised. The FK column needs no new RLS (insert/select/delete already governed by existing comentario policies; the column is just data).
**SQL (final):**
```sql
alter table public.comentario
  add column responde_a uuid references public.comentario(id) on delete cascade;
-- optional perf index for tree reads on busy publications:
create index if not exists comentario_responde_a_idx on public.comentario(responde_a);
```
Index is OPTIONAL (MVP volumes are tiny; the read filters by publicacion_id, not responde_a). Decide at apply time based on advisor output.

## ADR-2 — Dedicated getComentariosArbol over extending getPublicacion
**Decision:** New `getComentariosArbol(publicacionId)` in `lib/data/comentarios.ts`. Keep `getPublicacion`'s embedded `comentario(*)` AS-IS (backward compat); the page STOPS using it for comments.
**Rationale:** supabase-js `referencedTable` ordering can't express "roots desc + replies asc" in one embedded select; `getPublicacion` already carries 3 joins (SRP). One flat query + in-memory sort is clean, isolated, testable.
**Rejected:** extend `getPublicacion` embed (ordering impossible, high coupling); two queries (roots + replies) — unnecessary, one flat fetch + grouping is O(n) and simpler.
**Signature & return:**
```ts
export async function getComentariosArbol(
  publicacionId: string,
): Promise<{ data: { arbol: ComentarioArbol[]; total: number } | null; error: unknown }>
```
**The one query:**
```ts
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from('comentario')
  .select('*, usuario(id, nombre)')
  .eq('publicacion_id', publicacionId)
  .order('creado_en', { ascending: true })   // replies end up asc naturally
```
**In-memory grouping (O(n)):**
1. If error → `{ data: null, error }`. If no rows → `{ data: { arbol: [], total: 0 }, error: null }`.
2. `total = data.length` (flat count = roots + replies — the truthful heading count).
3. Build `Map<rootId, ComentarioConUsuario[]>` for replies; collect roots (`responde_a === null`).
4. Attach: each root gets `respuestas = repliesByRoot.get(root.id) ?? []` (already asc from query order).
5. Sort roots `creado_en` DESC (newest thread first); replies stay ASC. Use `toSorted` for immutability.
6. Return `{ data: { arbol, total }, error: null }`.
   Defensive: a reply whose `responde_a` has no matching root in this publication is dropped from the tree (can only happen via out-of-band depth-3 insert — see Risks). It still counts in `total` because total is the raw flat length; this is acceptable and documented.

## ADR-3 — POST handler: optional responde_a, single pre-insert SELECT, re-parent
**Decision:** Extend POST only (GET + DELETE untouched). Read optional `responde_a` from body. `autor_id` ALWAYS from `supabase.auth.getUser()` — never the body.
**Exact logic (insert order, after existing auth + presence + length checks):**
```
const { publicacion_id, contenido, responde_a } = body
// existing: unauthorized() if no user; validationError if !publicacion_id || !contenido; length>250
let efectivoRespondeA: string | null = null
if (responde_a) {
  const { data: padre, error: padreErr } = await supabase
    .from('comentario')
    .select('id, publicacion_id, responde_a')
    .eq('id', responde_a)
    .maybeSingle()
  if (padreErr) return handleError(padreErr)
  if (!padre) return validationError('El comentario al que respondés no existe.')
  if (padre.publicacion_id !== publicacion_id)
    return validationError('No podés responder a un comentario de otra publicación.')
  // re-parent: if target is itself a reply, anchor to ITS root → enforces depth 2
  efectivoRespondeA = padre.responde_a ?? padre.id
}
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from('comentario')
  .insert({ publicacion_id, contenido, autor_id: user.id, responde_a: efectivoRespondeA })
  .select()
  .single()
if (error) return handleError(error)
return jsonOk({ comentario: data }, 201)
```
**Rationale:** ONE extra query suffices. Because every insert re-parents to root, any existing `padre.responde_a` is already a root, so one level of chasing is exact. `maybeSingle()` (not `.single()`) so "not found" returns null instead of a PGRST116 error → clean 400 via our own `validationError`.
**Error/status mapping (contract preserved):**
- not found / cross-publication → **400** `validation_error` (creation contract, NOT a 404 lookup) via `validationError()`.
- RLS denies insert (42501) → 403, unique (23505) → 409, P0001 → 400, no JWT → 401, other → 500 — all via existing `handleError`.
**Rejected:** validating in the client (insecure, duplicates ownership logic — forbidden); recursive root-chasing (unnecessary given the invariant); 404 for not-found (wrong contract — this endpoint creates, it doesn't look up).

## ADR-4 — DTO design & location
**Decision:** all types in `lib/types/database.ts`.
```ts
export type Comentario = {
  id: string
  contenido: string
  publicacion_id: string
  autor_id: string
  responde_a: string | null   // NEW
  creado_en: string
  usuario?: Pick<Usuario, 'id' | 'nombre'> | null   // widen to | null (components already assume this)
}
export type ComentarioConUsuario = Comentario & {
  usuario?: Pick<Usuario, 'id' | 'nombre'> | null
}
export type ComentarioArbol = ComentarioConUsuario & {
  respuestas: ComentarioConUsuario[]
}
```
- Widen `usuario` to `| null` on `Comentario` so the inline `& { usuario?: … | null }` casts in the page/list can be dropped (current code patches this at every call site — consolidate it on the DTO).
- `PublicacionDetalle.comentario` stays (its rows now carry `responde_a` for free via the spread). No removal needed; page just stops reading it.
- `MAX_COMENTARIO_LEN = 250` could be hoisted to a shared const, but that's optional polish — not required by the design.

## ADR-5 — ComentarioList becomes the sole client boundary
**Decision:** `'use client'`. Props `{ comentarios: ComentarioArbol[]; publicacionId: string; isAuthenticated: boolean }`.
(Note: `publicacionId` is REQUIRED by the design even though the proposal listed only two props — the inline `ComentarioForm` needs it. Pass it from the page.)
**State & ownership:**
- `const [replyingTo, setReplyingTo] = useState<string | null>(null)`
- `const router = useRouter()` — refresh ownership MOVES here for the inline reply path.
**Markup (depth 2, NO recursion):**
- Outer `<ul>` of roots (current markup, reused).
- Inside each root `<li>`: existing author/time/contenido block, THEN
  - if `isAuthenticated`: a "Responder" toggle button → `setReplyingTo(replyingTo === c.id ? null : c.id)` (toggles).
  - if `replyingTo === c.id`: inline `<ComentarioForm publicacionId={publicacionId} respondaA={c.id} onSuccess={() => { setReplyingTo(null); router.refresh() }} />`.
  - if `c.respuestas.length > 0`: a nested `<ul className="ml-6 mt-3 …">` rendering each reply (author/time/contenido ONLY — NO "Responder" on replies, since depth-2).
**Boundary check (RSC leak):** imports allowed = `Link` (next/link), `useState`/`useRouter`, types, `ComentarioForm`. FORBIDDEN: any `lib/data/*` or `lib/supabase/server` import (server-only). Verify none leak after adding `'use client'`. Empty-state ("Sé el primero en comentar") stays.
**Rejected:** keep ComentarioList as RSC + separate `ReplyButton` client island per comment — more fragmentation, no gain; ComentarioList is a leaf so client cost is negligible.

## ADR-6 — ComentarioForm stays the shared form
**Decision:** add `respondaA?: string | null` and `onSuccess?: () => void`. Existing root usage unchanged (no new props).
- POST body: `{ publicacion_id, contenido, ...(respondaA ? { responde_a: respondaA } : {}) }`.
- On success: `setContenido('')`; if `onSuccess` provided → call it (it handles collapse + refresh for the reply case); else → `router.refresh()` (root case, current behavior). This avoids a double refresh.
- When `respondaA` set: label → "Tu respuesta", placeholder → "Escribí tu respuesta…", button → "Responder". Otherwise current copy.
- Keep `Field`, `ApiError` handling, `maxLength={250}` as-is.

## ADR-7 — Page integration
**Decision:**
- Add `getComentariosArbol(id)` to the existing parallel fetch region. NOTE: the current page does sequential `await`s (getLikesInfo, then getIsGuardado, …) NOT a single `Promise.all`. The design's intent is to AVOID adding a new waterfall: fold `getComentariosArbol(id)` into a `Promise.all` together with the independent `getLikesInfo`/`getIsGuardado` calls (it depends only on `id`, so it can start as early as after session resolve). Do not block it behind author-only fetches.
- Replace line 49 `const comentarios = (data.comentario ?? [])` with destructuring from `getComentariosArbol`:
  `const { data: comentariosData } = await getComentariosArbol(id)` → `const arbol = comentariosData?.arbol ?? []`, `const totalComentarios = comentariosData?.total ?? 0`.
- Heading: `Comentarios ({totalComentarios})` (was `{comentarios.length}`).
- `<ComentarioList comentarios={arbol} publicacionId={id} isAuthenticated={isAuthenticated} />`.
- Root form block (`isAuthenticated`) and anonymous "Iniciá sesión para comentar" block: UNCHANGED.
- Drop the now-unused inline `Comentario & { usuario… }` cast at line 49 once the DTO is widened.

## ADR-8 — Docs sync (mandatory, same change)
- **Vitrina_BD_Conexion_Backend.md:** add `responde_a uuid? FK→comentario(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` to the `comentario` table; add a `comentarios_hilos` entry to the documented ADITIVE exceptions block (mirroring the recomendacion/admin-elimina notes); note self-referential cascade (deleting a root removes its replies).
- **Vitrina_Especificaciones_APIs.md:** POST `/api/comentarios` (§comentarios / §4.4) — add optional `responde_a?: uuid` to payload; document validation (existence→400, cross-publication→400, re-parent-to-root semantics); §8 DTO table → `comentario` gets `responde_a uuid?`.
- **Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md §3.2:** ComentarioList now `'use client'`, 2-level thread list, props `isAuthenticated` + `publicacionId`, "Responder" on roots only; ComentarioForm gains `respondaA?` + `onSuccess?` (inline reply reuse).

## Trade-offs & non-mitigations
- **Depth-3 via direct DB insert is NOT mitigated** (deliberate). Re-parenting chases ONE level; it relies on the API being the only writer. A row inserted directly to the DB pointing at a reply (not a root) would, on read, fail to match any root in the Map and be DROPPED from the rendered tree (it still counts in `total`). Acceptable for MVP: all writes go through the handler which enforces depth 2; documented, not defended with a trigger (triggers are out of scope / forbidden).
- **Heading total counts orphaned/dropped replies** (total = raw flat length). Truthful "how many comments exist" even if one is not renderable. Alternative (count only rendered nodes) was rejected as more code for a case that can't occur via the API.
- **`getPublicacion` still over-fetches comments** (its embedded `comentario(*)` join remains for backward compat). Minor redundant fetch on the detail page; chosen over a riskier edit to a shared multi-join read. Can be trimmed later if profiling shows it matters.
- **No optimistic UI / pagination** — out of scope; `router.refresh()` round-trip is acceptable at MVP volumes.
- **maybeSingle vs single** in POST: `.maybeSingle()` deliberately chosen so not-found is null (clean 400), not a thrown PGRST116.

## Verification hooks (for tasks/verify phases)
1. Reply-to-reply stores ROOT id in `responde_a` (depth stays 2).
2. Cascade: deleting a root removes replies (existing DELETE handler + FK).
3. Cross-publication `responde_a` → 400 `validation_error`.
4. Anonymous: full threads visible, zero "Responder" buttons, "Iniciá sesión" prompt intact.
5. Heading count = roots + replies.
6. No server-only import leaks into `ComentarioList` after `'use client'`.

**Learned:** Two ground-truth deltas vs the proposal that the design corrects: (a) the page heading reads `getPublicacion`'s embedded `comentario`, not a separate flat fetch — so integration must replace BOTH the count source and the list source; (b) the `Comentario` DTO lacks `| null` on `usuario` (call sites patch it inline) — widen the DTO to consolidate. Also: ComentarioList needs `publicacionId` (3rd prop) for the inline form, which the 2-prop proposal omitted.

observations.title: sdd/comentarios-hilos/tasks
observations.content:
# Tasks — comentarios-hilos (2-level reply threads)

Generated: 2026-06-23. Derived from spec (#130) and design (#131).

---

## Execution order legend
- **[SEQ]** — must run after all predecessors complete
- **[PAR]** — can run in parallel with siblings at the same group level
- Numbers denote strict ordering across groups; letters denote parallelism within a group.

---

## Group 1 — DB migration (blocks everything)

### T-01 [SEQ] · Schema: add responde_a FK column
**Spec:** §3.1, §7 · **Design:** ADR-1

- Using Supabase MCP `execute_sql`, run iteratively until correct:
  ```sql
  alter table public.comentario
    add column responde_a uuid references public.comentario(id) on delete cascade;
  ```
- Verify column exists with a `select` query against `information_schema.columns` WHERE table_name = 'comentario'.
- Run `get_advisors` (security + performance advisors) after adding the column.
- Based on advisor output, decide whether to add the optional index:
  ```sql
  create index if not exists comentario_responde_a_idx
    on public.comentario(responde_a);
  ```
  (Add if advisor flags missing index or if any non-trivial load is anticipated; skip if advisors are clean and MVP volumes are tiny.)
- Capture final SQL in a migration note (or `supabase db pull` if CLI is available). Do NOT call `apply_migration` more than once.

**Files affected:** DB only (no source file)
**Blocks:** T-02, T-03, T-04

---

## Group 2 — Types (can start once T-01 is done; T-02a and T-02b are independent of each other)

### T-02a [PAR] · DTO: widen Comentario + add ComentarioArbol types
**Spec:** §2.1–§2.3 · **Design:** ADR-4
**File:** `lib/types/database.ts`

- Add `responde_a: string | null` to the `Comentario` type/interface.
- Widen the `usuario` field on `Comentario` to `Pick<Usuario, 'id' | 'nombre'> | null` (currently non-nullable at some definition; widen so call-site inline casts can be dropped).
- Add `ComentarioConUsuario` type: `Comentario & { usuario?: Pick<Usuario, 'id' | 'nombre'> | null }` (if not already present as a named type — verify first).
- Add `ComentarioArbol` type: `ComentarioConUsuario & { respuestas: ComentarioConUsuario[] }`.
- Do NOT remove or rename existing `Comentario` usage; this is additive.

**Blocks:** T-03, T-05, T-06

### T-02b [PAR] · (No dependency on T-02a) — placeholder; T-02a is the only type task.

_(No separate T-02b — T-02a covers all DTO work. Group 2 has a single task.)_

---

## Group 3 — Data layer (depends on T-01 + T-02a)

### T-03 [SEQ] · Data layer: getComentariosArbol in lib/data/comentarios.ts
**Spec:** §5.1 · **Design:** ADR-2
**File:** `lib/data/comentarios.ts`

- Add (do NOT replace existing functions) `getComentariosArbol(publicacionId: string)` as a named export.
- Return type: `Promise<{ data: { arbol: ComentarioArbol[]; total: number } | null; error: unknown }>`.
- ONE supabase-js query:
  ```ts
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('comentario')
    .select('*, usuario(id, nombre)')
    .eq('publicacion_id', publicacionId)
    .order('creado_en', { ascending: true })
  ```
- On error → `{ data: null, error }`.
- On empty → `{ data: { arbol: [], total: 0 }, error: null }`.
- `total = data.length` (flat, captured before grouping).
- Build `Map<rootId, ComentarioConUsuario[]>` for replies (`responde_a !== null`).
- Collect roots (`responde_a === null`), attach `respuestas` array.
- Sort roots `creado_en DESC` (use `toSorted` for immutability; replies stay ASC from query).
- Return `{ data: { arbol, total }, error: null }`.
- Defensive: replies whose `responde_a` matches no root in this publication are silently dropped from the tree (cannot happen via the API, but safe to guard).
- This file is SERVER-ONLY; do NOT add `'use client'`.

**Blocks:** T-07

---

## Group 4 — API mutation (depends on T-01 + T-02a; parallel with T-03)

### T-04 [SEQ] · POST handler: optional responde_a + re-parent logic
**Spec:** §4.1–§4.3, S-03–S-07 · **Design:** ADR-3
**File:** `app/api/comentarios/route.ts`

- Extend the POST export ONLY. GET path is untouched.
- Read `responde_a` (optional) from body alongside existing `publicacion_id` + `contenido`.
- `autor_id` ALWAYS from `supabase.auth.getUser()` — never from body (existing invariant, reinforce).
- After existing auth + presence + length checks, add re-parent block:
  ```
  let efectivoRespondeA: string | null = null
  if (responde_a) {
    const { data: padre, error: padreErr } = await supabase
      .from('comentario')
      .select('id, publicacion_id, responde_a')
      .eq('id', responde_a)
      .maybeSingle()
    if (padreErr) return handleError(padreErr)
    if (!padre) return validationError('El comentario al que respondés no existe.')
    if (padre.publicacion_id !== publicacion_id)
      return validationError('No podés responder a un comentario de otra publicación.')
    efectivoRespondeA = padre.responde_a ?? padre.id   // re-parent to root
  }
  ```
- Insert with `responde_a: efectivoRespondeA`.
- Use `.maybeSingle()` (not `.single()`) on the pre-insert SELECT.
- Error mapping: not-found / cross-pub → 400 `validation_error`; rest via existing `handleError`.
- Do NOT touch: GET path, DELETE handler in `[id]/route.ts`.

**Blocks:** T-05 (testing path), T-07 (integration)

---

## Group 5 — UI components (T-05 and T-06 are parallel; depend on T-02a)

### T-05 [PAR] · ComentarioForm: add respondaA + onSuccess props
**Spec:** §6.6 · **Design:** ADR-6
**File:** `components/publicacion/ComentarioForm.tsx`

- Add optional props: `respondaA?: string | null` and `onSuccess?: () => void`.
- POST body: `{ publicacion_id, contenido, ...(respondaA ? { responde_a: respondaA } : {}) }`.
- On success: call `onSuccess()` if provided (caller handles collapse + refresh); otherwise `router.refresh()` (root form — current behavior). Do NOT double-refresh.
- When `respondaA` is set, switch copy: label → "Tu respuesta", placeholder → "Escribí tu respuesta…", button → "Responder".
- When `respondaA` is absent: all copy and behavior unchanged from baseline.
- Keep `maxLength={250}`, existing field, `ApiError` display, and form state as-is.

**Blocks:** T-06, T-07

### T-06 [PAR] · ComentarioList: convert to client component with reply state
**Spec:** §6.2–§6.5 · **Design:** ADR-5
**File:** `components/publicacion/ComentarioList.tsx`

- Add `'use client'` directive at top of file.
- Change props signature to: `{ comentarios: ComentarioArbol[]; publicacionId: string; isAuthenticated: boolean }`.
- Add state: `const [replyingTo, setReplyingTo] = useState<string | null>(null)`.
- Add `const router = useRouter()` — refresh ownership moves here for inline replies.
- Outer `<ul>` renders roots (existing markup reused where possible).
- Inside each root `<li>`:
  - Existing author/time/contenido block.
  - If `isAuthenticated`: toggle button "Responder" → `setReplyingTo(replyingTo === c.id ? null : c.id)` (toggles; collapses if same root clicked again).
  - If `replyingTo === c.id`: inline `<ComentarioForm publicacionId={publicacionId} respondaA={c.id} onSuccess={() => { setReplyingTo(null); router.refresh() }} />`.
  - If `c.respuestas.length > 0`: nested `<ul className="ml-6 mt-3 …">` rendering each reply (author/time/contenido ONLY — NO "Responder" button on replies — depth-2 cap).
- Anonymous path: no "Responder" button anywhere; empty-state "Sé el primero en comentar" preserved.
- RSC leak check: after adding `'use client'`, verify NO imports from `lib/data/*` or `lib/supabase/server` remain in this file.

**Blocks:** T-07

---

## Group 6 — Page integration (depends on T-03, T-04, T-05, T-06 all complete)

### T-07 [SEQ] · Page: integrate getComentariosArbol, fix heading count, pass new props
**Spec:** §6.1, S-08–S-12 · **Design:** ADR-7
**File:** `app/(main)/publicacion/[id]/page.tsx`

- Import `getComentariosArbol` from `lib/data/comentarios.ts`.
- Fold `getComentariosArbol(id)` into a `Promise.all` together with the independent `getLikesInfo`/`getIsGuardado` calls (depends only on `id`; must NOT be blocked behind author-only fetches). This replaces the current sequential waterfall pattern for these calls.
- Destructure result: `const { data: comentariosData } = await …` → `const arbol = comentariosData?.arbol ?? []`, `const totalComentarios = comentariosData?.total ?? 0`.
- Replace the heading's comment count source (currently `comentarios.length`) with `totalComentarios`.
- Update `<ComentarioList>` call site: pass `comentarios={arbol}`, `publicacionId={id}`, `isAuthenticated={isAuthenticated}`.
- Remove the now-unused inline `Comentario & { usuario?: … }` cast at the line that read `data.comentario` (once DTO is widened in T-02a).
- Keep: root form block (`isAuthenticated`), anonymous "Iniciá sesión para comentar" block — unchanged.
- Keep: `getPublicacion`'s embedded `comentario(*)` select — NOT modified (backward compat; the page just stops using its `comentario` field for list/count).

**Blocks:** T-08 (docs), T-09 (verification)

---

## Group 7 — Docs sync (parallel with T-09; both depend on T-07)

### T-08 [PAR] · Docs: update all three promts/ files
**Spec:** §10 · **Design:** ADR-8
**Files:** `promts/Vitrina_BD_Conexion_Backend.md`, `promts/Vitrina_Especificaciones_APIs.md`, `promts/Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md`

#### BD doc
- Add `responde_a uuid? FK→comentario(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` to the `comentario` table description.
- Add an additive-exception entry (mirroring recomendacion-publicacion and admin-elimina-publicacion notes): "comentarios-hilos: `responde_a` column, self-referential FK, cascade. No RLS/RPC/policy change."
- Note: deleting a root comment cascades to all its replies automatically.

#### APIs doc
- POST `/api/comentarios`: add optional `responde_a?: uuid` to payload table.
- Document validation rules: existence check (→ 400), cross-publication check (→ 400), re-parent-to-root semantics.
- §8 DTO table: add `responde_a: uuid | null` to `comentario` DTO; add `ComentarioArbol` type entry.

#### Pantallas/Componentes doc §3.2
- `ComentarioList`: now `'use client'`; props `{ comentarios: ComentarioArbol[]; publicacionId: string; isAuthenticated: boolean }`; 2-level thread with "Responder" on roots only; `replyingTo` state; only one reply form open at a time.
- `ComentarioForm`: gains `respondaA?: string | null` and `onSuccess?: () => void`; inline reply reuse via these props.
- Detail page heading: now bound to `total` from `getComentariosArbol`, not `arbol.length`.

---

## Group 8 — Verification (parallel with T-08; depends on T-07)

### T-09a [PAR] · Static checks: tsc + lint
**Spec:** §9 out-of-scope invariants · **Design:** all ADRs

- Run `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`. All type errors must be zero.
- Run `pnpm lint`. All lint errors must be zero.
- Pay special attention to: ComentarioList `'use client'` import leak (no `lib/data` or `lib/supabase/server`); async page param access (Next.js 16 — `await props.params`); Tailwind v4 class syntax (no `[--var]` shorthand).

### T-09b [PAR] · Spec checks: 4 core acceptance scenarios
**Spec:** S-03, S-04, S-07, S-10 · **Design:** verification hooks

Verify via Supabase MCP `execute_sql` + `webapp-testing` skill as applicable:

1. **S-03 reply-to-reply → root anchor:** POST a reply to a reply; assert stored `responde_a` = root id (not the intermediate reply id). Use `execute_sql` to inspect the inserted row.
2. **S-13 cascade delete:** DELETE a root comment; assert all its replies are gone from `comentario` table. Use `execute_sql` SELECT to confirm absence.
3. **S-04 cross-publication responde_a → 400:** POST with `responde_a` from a different `publicacion_id`; assert API returns 400 `validation_error` and no row inserted.
4. **S-10 anonymous no Responder button:** Load the publication detail page without a session (or with `isAuthenticated=false`); assert no "Responder" button rendered anywhere in the tree; assert "Iniciá sesión para comentar" prompt visible. Use webapp-testing (screenshot / DOM assertion).

**Bonus (if time allows, not blocking):**
- S-08 heading count = roots + replies (DOM assertion).
- S-09 render order: C2 above C1 (DESC roots), R1 above R2 inside C1 (ASC replies).
- S-11 Responder only on roots (DOM assertion: root has button, reply li has none).

---

## Dependency graph (compact)

```
T-01 ──┬──► T-02a ──┬──► T-03 ──────────────────────┐
       │            ├──► T-04 ────────────────────────┤
       │            ├──► T-05 ──┐                     ▼
       │            └──► T-06 ──┴────────────────► T-07 ──┬──► T-08 [PAR]
       │                                                   └──► T-09a [PAR]
       │                                                        T-09b [PAR]
       └── (T-03/T-04 also depend on T-01 via DB schema)
```

Strictly sequential chain: T-01 → T-02a → {T-03, T-04, T-05, T-06 in parallel} → T-07 → {T-08, T-09a, T-09b in parallel}

---

## Review Workload Forecast

| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| T-01 DB migration | ~8 lines SQL |
| T-02a DTO additions | ~15 lines |
| T-03 getComentariosArbol | ~50 lines |
| T-04 POST handler extension | ~35 lines |
| T-05 ComentarioForm props | ~25 lines |
| T-06 ComentarioList rewrite | ~70 lines |
| T-07 Page integration | ~30 lines |
| T-08 Docs sync (3 files) | ~60 lines prose |
| T-09a/b Verification | no prod code |
| **Total estimated changed lines** | **~293 lines** |

- **400-line budget risk: Low** (~293 lines estimated, well under 400)
- **Chained PRs recommended: No** — single PR fits comfortably within the review budget
- **Decision needed before apply: No** — proceed with `sdd-apply` as a single PR

  - S-13 cascade delete (DB inspect)

- Page was using sequential `await`s (not `Promise.all`). Folded `getComentariosArbol` into a `Promise.all` alongside `getLikesInfo`/`getIsGuardado` — eliminates waterfall.
- `getPublicacion`'s embedded `comentario(*)` select is intentionally preserved (backward compat) even though the page no longer uses it for list/count. The inline `Comentario & { usuario?... }` cast at line 49 was removed.
- `ComentarioList` imports only: `useState`, `useRouter`, `Link` (next/link), `ComentarioForm`, and types — no server-only leaks.
- `toSorted` used for immutable root sort (Node 20+ / ES2023 — already in use in the repo via Next.js 16).

observations.title: sdd/tendencias-areas-ctas/explore
observations.content:
## SDD Explore — tendencias-areas-ctas

### Scope
Combined change covering spec tasks 2, 3, 4 from `promts/promts/promt2.md`:
- Feature 2: Trending feed (`feed_trending` view, `getTrendingFeed`, home section)
- Feature 3: Area landing pages `/area/[slug]` + `/areas` index + sitemap
- Feature 4: Contextual CTAs for anonymous users

---

## Feature 2 — Trending Feed

### `feed_publicaciones` columns (confirmed from docs + DTO)

The view exposes: `id, autor_id, autor_nombre, titulo, resumen, archivo_url, tipo, creado_en, likes (int), comentarios (int), obra_autor_externo, url_externa`.
Does NOT expose `bloqueada` (filtered away with `WHERE p.bloqueada = false`).
The `FeedPublicacion` DTO in `lib/types/database.ts` already has all these fields except `likes` and `comentarios` (those two are NOT in the DTO currently — they are only used internally). The view has them for the `score` formula.

**`feed_trending` view:**
```sql
create view feed_trending
with (security_invoker = true) as
select
  f.*,
  (f.likes + f.comentarios)::numeric
    / power(extract(epoch from (now() - f.creado_en)) / 3600 + 2, 1.6)
    as score
from feed_publicaciones f;
```
Inherits `WHERE bloqueada = false` and `security_invoker = true` from parent view.
Requires confirming anon SELECT grant on the new view — since it inherits from `feed_publicaciones` which already has anon access, RLS is inherited via `security_invoker`. But the Data API grant on the new view itself must be confirmed (need to GRANT SELECT ON feed_trending TO anon, authenticated via Supabase MCP after creation).

### DTO decision: reuse or extend?

`feed_trending` adds a `score float8` column to all columns of `feed_publicaciones`.
Decision: **do NOT expose `score` in the public DTO**. `score` is an implementation detail of ranking — it changes every second and has no UI value.

`FeedPublicacion` DTO can be reused as-is for `getTrendingFeed`. The supabase-js call can simply `select('*')` against `feed_trending` and the extra `score` column is ignored by TypeScript (it's on the supabase return, not in the DTO). Alternatively, select only the `feed_publicaciones` columns explicitly.

**Recommendation**: Select `id,titulo,resumen,tipo,archivo_url,autor_id,autor_nombre,obra_autor_externo,url_externa,creado_en` explicitly (no `score`, no `likes`, no `comentarios`). This is safe, avoids leaking ranking internals, and lets `FeedPublicacion` be reused unchanged.

### `getTrendingFeed` signature

```ts
// lib/data/trending.ts  (NEW FILE)
export async function getTrendingFeed({
  limit = 10,
  offset = 0,
}: {
  limit?: number
  offset?: number
} = {}): Promise<{ data: FeedPublicacion[] | null; error: unknown }>
```

Query: `.from('feed_trending').select('<explicit cols>').order('score', { ascending: false }).range(offset, offset + limit - 1)`.
No `tipo` filter (trending is always global — spec does not mention per-tipo trending).
No offset pagination needed for the home section (always limit=10, no paginate), but the signature supports it for future use.

### Home page integration

**Design question:** show trending section always, or only when no area/tipo filter is active?

Analysis:
- When `area` or `tipo` filter is active, the user has explicitly narrowed the feed. Showing a global trending section above a filtered view creates confusion (trending could contain different areas/tipos than the filter).
- The spec says "ARRIBA del feed normal en `/`" without explicit filter-conditional language, but the intent is discoverable engagement, not noise.

**Recommendation:** Show the trending section **only when no `area` and no `tipo` filter is active** (i.e., the default unfiltered home view). This matches "above the normal feed" naturally — when you filter, the filtered feed IS the primary intent.

Implementation: in `app/(main)/page.tsx`, conditionally fetch `getTrendingFeed` in parallel with `getFeed` (via `Promise.all`) when `!area && !tipo`. Map to `PublicacionCardData` same way as `getFeed` (using `autor_nombre`). Render a new `<TrendingSection>` server component (or inline JSX) above `FeedFilters`.

**Items:** limit=10 per spec. No pagination for trending section.

**Empty state:** use `EmptyState` with title "No hay tendencias aún" (few/no publications yet).

### Files to create/edit (Feature 2)
- CREATE: `lib/data/trending.ts` — `getTrendingFeed()`
- EDIT: `app/(main)/page.tsx` — add conditional parallel fetch + TrendingSection render
- CREATE: `components/feed/TrendingSection.tsx` — renders a titled list reusing FeedList/cards
- EDIT: `lib/types/database.ts` — no change needed (FeedPublicacion reused as-is)
- DB migration via Supabase MCP: CREATE VIEW feed_trending + GRANT SELECT

### Docs to update (Feature 2)
- `Vitrina_BD_Conexion_Backend.md` — add `feed_trending` view description
- `Vitrina_Especificaciones_APIs.md` — add feed_trending endpoint in §4.3
- `Vitrina_Pantallas_Componentes.md` — add TrendingSection in home page description

### Gotchas (Feature 2)
- `score` is computed at query time — no materialized view needed at current scale but document the pg_cron path as a comment in the migration SQL.
- The GRANT on the view must be explicit — inheriting from `feed_publicaciones` covers RLS rows but not the API layer grant. Confirm via Supabase MCP after creating the view.
- `getTrendingFeed` and `getFeed` fetched in `Promise.all` — no waterfall.

---

## Feature 3 — Area landing `/area/[slug]`

### Slug strategy: static curated map vs runtime derivation

**Option A — Static curated map in `lib/constants/areas.ts`**
- Define `AREA_SLUG_MAP: Record<string, string>` (area → slug) and reverse `SLUG_AREA_MAP: Record<string, string>` (slug → area).
- Slugs computed once at build time. `generateStaticParams` returns the curated list.
- Stable canonical URLs even if `tag.area` strings change in DB.
- Risk: map can go out of sync if new areas are added in DB but not in the constant.

**Option B — Runtime derivation from `getDistinctAreas()`**
- Compute slug at runtime from the area string (lowercase, strip accents, spaces → hyphens).
- `generateStaticParams` calls `getDistinctAreas()` at build time.
- Always in sync with DB.
- Risk: if a tag area name changes, its slug (and URL) changes — breaking SEO. Canonical URL instability.

**Recommendation: Option A (static curated map)**.
Reasons:
1. `tag.area` is a free-form string managed by admins. The set of areas is small and stable (academic disciplines don't change often).
2. SEO canonical URL stability is critical — a DB value change must NOT silently change a URL.
3. `generateStaticParams` works cleanly with a static map at build time (no Supabase call needed at build if we embed the map — though a call is fine too).
4. The map doubles as the source of truth for the `/areas` index page (no extra DB call needed to enumerate valid areas).

**Map design in `lib/constants/areas.ts`:**
```ts
export const AREA_TO_SLUG: Record<string, string> = {
  'Biología': 'biologia',
  'Química': 'quimica',
  'Historia': 'historia',
  // ... all known areas
}
export const SLUG_TO_AREA: Record<string, string> = Object.fromEntries(
  Object.entries(AREA_TO_SLUG).map(([area, slug]) => [slug, area])
)
```
Slug conventions: lowercase, no accents (NFD normalize + strip combining chars), spaces → hyphens, no special chars.
Helper `areaToSlug(area: string): string | undefined` for checking existence.

**Bootstrapping the map:** at implementation time, call `getDistinctAreas()` once to get the current list, then manually curate the map. This is a one-time effort.

### `getDistinctAreas()` — new data function

Needed for:
1. `generateStaticParams` (enumerate areas with ≥3 publications)
2. `/areas` index page
3. Building the curated map initially

```ts
// lib/data/areas.ts  (NEW FILE)
export async function getDistinctAreas(): Promise<{
  data: { area: string; count: number }[] | null
  error: unknown
}>
```

Implementation: supabase-js cannot do `GROUP BY` natively via the PostgREST API without an RPC or view. Options:

**Option A**: Direct Supabase query using `publicacion_tag` join to `tag` with a count approach. The cleanest is a head count query per area. But with many areas, N queries is bad.

**Option B**: Fetch all distinct areas from `tag` table (already available via `getTags()`), then for each area do a `.select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true })` on `publicacion_tag!inner(tag!inner(area))`. Still N queries.

**Option C**: Create a simple database view or RPC `get_area_counts()` that returns `(area text, count bigint)`. Clean, single query.

**Option D**: Use `getTags()` to get all tags (each has an `area`), then use supabase-js to count publications per tag group. But that doesn't count unique publications per area (a publication tagged with two tags in same area would double-count).

**Recommendation: Option C — a lightweight RPC `get_area_counts()`** that returns distinct areas with their publication counts. This is a single query, efficient, and avoids N+1. The RPC is read-only, no auth logic needed, accessible to anon.

SQL for the RPC (aditiva):
```sql
create or replace function get_area_counts()
```
