- One table plus HTML5 `form="form-devolucion-N"` attributes on the checkboxes/textarea/submit -> valid, but it relies on a feature most readers do not know, and the first person who "fixes" it by wrapping the table in the form re-creates the exact hazard above.

Two tables also carry different columns honestly: A shows checkbox / título / folio; B shows título / folio / fecha de devolución / notas / acción.

```hbs
<form method="POST" action="/solicitudes/devoluciones" id="form-devolucion-{{this.solicitud_id}}" data-devolucion-form>
  <input type="hidden" name="_csrf" value="{{../csrfToken}}" />
  <input type="hidden" name="solicitud_id" value="{{this.solicitud_id}}" />
  <input type="hidden" name="curp_filtro" value="{{../filtroCurp}}" />
  <input type="hidden" name="codigo_filtro" value="{{../filtroCodigo}}" />

  <div class="table-wrap"> ... <input type="checkbox" name="linea_id[]" value="{{this.lineaId}}" /> ... </div>

  <div class="field full" style="margin-top: 12px;">
    <label for="notas-{{../solicitud_id}}">Notas (opcional)</label>
    <textarea id="notas-{{../solicitud_id}}" name="notas" rows="2" maxlength="500"></textarea>
  </div>
  <span class="field-error" data-devolucion-error></span>

  <div class="dialog-actions">
    <button class="btn btn-green-outline" type="submit">
      <span class="material-symbols-outlined">assignment_turned_in</span> Registrar devolución
    </button>
  </div>
</form>
```
Checkbox name is `linea_id[]`, mirroring `libro_id[]` in `solicitud-libros.hbs`. One `<textarea name="notas">` per group form — "one note per submission" scopes to the submission, and the submission is one solicitud.

Undo action in table B's `<td>`:
```hbs
<form method="POST" action="/solicitudes/devoluciones/{{this.lineaId}}/deshacer" class="inline-form" data-devolucion-undo>
  <input type="hidden" name="_csrf" value="{{../../csrfToken}}" />
  <input type="hidden" name="curp_filtro" value="{{../../filtroCurp}}" />
  <input type="hidden" name="codigo_filtro" value="{{../../filtroCodigo}}" />
  <button type="submit" class="chip-btn chip-orange">
    <span class="material-symbols-outlined">undo</span><span>Deshacer</span>
  </button>
</form>
```
The two hidden filter inputs are mandatory here, not a nicety: they are what keeps the post-undo re-render in mode B, and therefore what keeps a fully-returned solicitud on screen while it is being corrected.

**Orange `chip-orange` + `undo` icon.** Green and red are taken by aceptar/rechazar and blue by editar; orange is the design guide's warning token and reads as "corrective action", which is exactly what an undo is. `.chip-orange` does not exist in `styles.css` yet (only blue/green/red at lines 250-273) — add it in the same shape using `#f59e0b`, alongside `.mensaje-exito` (`--btn-green`) and `.mensaje-aviso` (`--btn-orange`), mirroring `.field-error`'s 12px form.

## 10. Client script — `public/js/devoluciones.js`

Same shell as the siblings: `'use strict'` + `DOMContentLoaded`, no inline handlers (CSP `scriptSrc` has no `'unsafe-inline'`), `Swal`/`bootstrap` already declared as browser globals in `eslint.config.js`.

**Collapse toggle generalized from 1 to N.** `solicitud-libros.js:114-126` hardcodes `getElementById('libros-collapse')` / `getElementById('libros-toggle')`. The generalization pairs each toggle with its target through the attribute Bootstrap itself already needs, so the id scheme lives in exactly one place (the view) and never has to be mirrored in JS:

```js
document.querySelectorAll('[data-devolucion-toggle]').forEach((toggle) => {
  const target = document.querySelector(toggle.dataset.bsTarget);
  if (!target) return;
  const icon = toggle.querySelector('.material-symbols-outlined');
  target.addEventListener('shown.bs.collapse', () => {
    toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    if (icon) icon.textContent = 'expand_less';
  });
  target.addEventListener('hidden.bs.collapse', () => {
    toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    if (icon) icon.textContent = 'expand_more';
  });
});
```
Listeners are bound per target, not delegated at `document` level — `shown.bs.collapse` bubbles, so a document-level listener would fire once per instance for every toggle.

**Per-form validation + confirm.** Checkboxes live inside their own form (§9), so scoping is `form.querySelectorAll`, no id lookups. `[data-devolucion-form]` simply matches nothing for a `soloDevueltos` card, so no guard is needed for the form-free case:

```js
document.querySelectorAll('[data-devolucion-form]').forEach((form) => {
  const errorEl = form.querySelector('[data-devolucion-error]');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const marcados = form.querySelectorAll('input[name="linea_id[]"]:checked');
    if (marcados.length === 0) {
      if (errorEl) errorEl.textContent = 'Selecciona al menos un libro para registrar la devolución.';
      return;
    }
    if (errorEl) errorEl.textContent = '';
    Swal.fire({
      title: '¿Registrar la devolución?',
      text: `Se marcarán ${marcados.length} libro(s) como devueltos y se restaurará su disponibilidad.`,
      icon: 'question', showCancelButton: true,
      confirmButtonText: 'Sí, registrar', cancelButtonText: 'Cancelar',
      reverseButtons: true, allowOutsideClick: false,
    }).then((result) => { if (result.isConfirmed) form.submit(); });
  });
});
```

**Undo confirm — copy constrained by the proposal.** It must not promise totals are restored:
```js
title: '¿Deshacer la devolución?',
text: 'El libro volverá a contar como préstamo activo y se descontará una copia disponible. El total de copias del catálogo no cambia.',
confirmButtonText: 'Sí, deshacer',
```
Bound over `[data-devolucion-undo]` with the same preventDefault -> confirm -> `form.submit()` shape as `solicitudes.js`. `form.submit()` does not re-fire the submit event, so there is no recursion — same as the existing script.

## 11. Migration — `scripts/migrate-solicitud-devoluciones.js`

Skeleton copied from `migrate-solicitud-multi-libro.js`: `require('dotenv').config()`, the defensive `process.env.TZ ||=` pin with its comment, `parseArgs(argv)` -> `{ dryRun }`, guarded-DDL constants, read-only `columnExists()` checks driving both the dry-run report and the live log lines, a closing nullability report, `await pool.close()`, and `main().catch(err => { console.error('Error al migrar:', err.message); process.exitCode = 1; })`.

```js
const ADD_COLUMN_FECHA_DEVOLUCION_SQL = `
IF NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA='dbo' AND TABLE_NAME='solicitud_libros' AND COLUMN_NAME='fecha_devolucion')
  ALTER TABLE dbo.solicitud_libros ADD fecha_devolucion DATETIME NULL;`;

const ADD_COLUMN_NOTAS_DEVOLUCION_SQL = `
IF NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA='dbo' AND TABLE_NAME='solicitud_libros' AND COLUMN_NAME='notas_devolucion')
  ALTER TABLE dbo.solicitud_libros ADD notas_devolucion VARCHAR(500) NULL;`;
```
`columnExists(name)` is the sibling's function with `TABLE_NAME` retargeted to `'solicitud_libros'`. Dropped from the copy: `CREATE TABLE`, both `CREATE INDEX`, `RESEED_IDENTITY`, both `sp_addextendedproperty`, and `BACKFILL` — the columns are nullable and mean "not returned", so a backfill would be writing a value that is already correct by absence.

**Exactly 2 columns. No third.** `devolucion_ajusto_total` was explicitly rejected by the user; re-verified by gate review in rev 2. Do not add attribution during apply.

**One addition over a blind copy: a `tableExists()` precondition that fails loudly.**
```js
if (!(await tableExists())) {
  console.error('dbo.solicitud_libros no existe. Ejecuta primero npm run migrate:solicitud-multi-libro.');
  process.exitCode = 1;
  return;
}
```
Without it a live run would throw a raw SQL error, and — worse — a `--dry-run` would report "se agregaría" for both columns and exit 0, i.e. a dry-run that lies about what a live run would do.

**No new index.** A filtered index on `(estatus, fecha_devolucion)` would help mode A's outstanding-lines subquery at scale, but the proposal fixed the migration surface at exactly 2 columns, `IX_sl_estatus` already exists, and an index is a separately reversible perf change. Recorded as a future lever, not smuggled in. Note that mode B does not use that subquery at all, so the lever only ever mattered for the default view.

`db/schema.sql` gets the same 2 columns inside `CREATE TABLE dbo.solicitud_libros` (no auto-sync exists between them). `db/seed-ci.sql` flips at least one seeded line to `'aceptada'` so the CI container has an outstanding loan to list — the current seed inserts every line as `'pendiente'`, which would render an empty devoluciones screen for the DAST/perf flows.

---
**Continues in `sdd/solicitud-devoluciones/design-parte-2` (obs #149): §12 test strategy, §13 decisions (D1-D21), §14 data flow, §15 integration points, §16 risks, §17 out of scope.**

observations.title: sdd/solicitud-devoluciones/design (parte 2 de 2)
observations.content:
# Technical Design: solicitud-devoluciones — PART 2 of 2

> **Continuation of observation #148 (`sdd/solicitud-devoluciones/design`).** Read #148 first — §1-§11 live there. Nothing here supersedes it.
> **REV 2 — gate-review rework.** The split boundary moved: this part now starts at §12 (it previously started mid-§14). Part 1 grew past the Engram 50,000-char save limit after the two-mode query fix, so §12 and §13 moved here and §14 is no longer split across observations. New in this part: test cases 26-31, decision D21, and updated §16 risk rows.

## 12. Test strategy

### 12.1 mockPool gap — confirmed, not theoretical

`resolveFakeQuery`'s UPDATE branch returns `{ rowsAffected: [updateRowsAffected] }` with **no `recordset`** (`test/helpers/mockPool.js:107-112`). Both write paths read `.recordset` from an `OUTPUT`-bearing UPDATE, so today every one of them would blow up on `undefined.length`. The existing generic SQL-verb dispatch is *not* sufficient; the proposal's and exploration's expectation is wrong on this point.

Minimal fix, in the mock's existing idiom:
```js
// UPDATE branch
if (updateError) throw updateError;
const affected = updateRowsAffected !== null
  ? updateRowsAffected
  : (updateOutputRows ? updateOutputRows.length : 1);
return updateOutputRows ? { recordset: updateOutputRows, rowsAffected: [affected] } : { rowsAffected: [affected] };
```
with `updateRowsAffected` re-defaulted from `1` to `null` in the destructuring so "not specified" becomes distinguishable. Behavior for every existing test is byte-identical (none pass `updateOutputRows`, so `affected` still resolves to 1).

Deriving `rowsAffected` from `updateOutputRows.length` follows the same philosophy as `countInsertValueTuples` — infer the count from the data instead of making every test restate it — and, critically, keeps a *mismatched* pair expressible by setting both explicitly, which is exactly the fixture the §6.1 consistency-check test needs. Update the file's JSDoc block, which documents every option.

**Rev 2 status: CONFIRMED.** Gate review independently verified the byte-identical claim against the existing suites. Keep this shape exactly as written during apply; do not "simplify" the `null` default back to `1`, which would silently collapse the mismatch fixture.

No other mock capability is needed: the list SELECT falls through to the generic `{ recordset: rows }` branch, and `createFakeTransaction`'s shared-request `sequence` already expresses "step 1 returns these OUTPUT rows, step 2 returns those".

### 12.2 New suite — `test/devoluciones.routes.test.js`

Copy the `withLogin` / `authenticatedAgent` pair from `test/solicitudes.routes.test.js:40-72`; it is defined only there (`auth.routes.test.js` and `libros.routes.test.js` each roll their own agent setup). Extracting a shared auth helper into `test/helpers/` would touch three existing suites and belongs to its own change.

Coverage, mapped to the proposal's success criteria:

| # | Case | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | GET with no filters lists only solicitudes with ≥1 outstanding line, grouped | mode A + grouping |
| 2 | GET by CURP / by codigo / by both (AND) — bind values asserted via `_inputs` | filters |
| 3 | GET malformed CURP -> 400, message, no SELECT issued | "message, not empty list" |
| 4 | GET malformed codigo -> 400, message | same |
| 5 | Lines with `estatus <> 'aceptada'` never render, **in either mode** | §5 query scoping |
| 6 | Returned lines land in table B with fecha + notas, outstanding in table A | two-bucket split |
| 7 | POST n of N -> only the n posted ids bound, siblings untouched | partial selection |
| 8 | POST -> `libros` UPDATE binds one `@deltaN` per distinct book | restore |
| 9 | **Overshoot: OUTPUT `totales_antes < totales_despues` -> orange aviso names the book and both counts** | self-heal + admin message |
| 10 | Mixed batch (1 book raises, 1 does not) -> aviso names only the raiser | aggregation across N |
| 11 | Re-submit with empty OUTPUT -> 200, neutral message, **no `libros` UPDATE issued at all** | idempotency |
| 12 | `rowsAffected` != OUTPUT length -> throws, rollback, 500 | §6.1 consistency guard |
| 13 | `libros` rowsAffected != K -> throws, rollback, 500 | §6.2 completeness guard |
| 14 | Two OUTPUT rows sharing a `libro_id` -> a single `@delta0 = 2` | §6.3 aggregation (unreachable under today's UNIQUE constraint — pins the guard, name says so) |
| 15 | Delta entries bound in ascending `libro_id` order | §6.4 deadlock ordering |
| 16 | notas persisted on every covered line; blank -> NULL; >500 -> 400 | note handling |
| 17 | `linea_id[]` empty / non-numeric / >30 -> 400 + message, no transaction | input hardening |
| 18 | Line from another solicitud -> filtered by `AND solicitud_id = @solicitudId`, no-op | scope guard |
| 19 | Undo happy path: both columns cleared, `copias_disponibles - 1` | undo |
| 20 | **Undo issues no statement touching `copias_totales` — including after an overshoot raise. Test name carries the accepted-inflation rationale.** | the load-bearing non-behavior |
| 21 | Undo at `copias_disponibles = 0` -> rollback asserted via `tx._rolledBack`, 409, no partial write | veto |
| 22 | Double undo -> 409, no-op | idempotency |
| 23 | Non-numeric `:id` -> 404 | param hardening |
| 24 | All 3 routes unauthenticated -> redirect to `/login`; both POSTs without `_csrf` -> rejected | auth/CSRF |
| 25 | POST re-render preserves `curp_filtro`/`codigo_filtro` in the refreshed forms | filter carry-through |
| **26** | **Unfiltered GET: a solicitud whose `aceptada` lines are ALL returned is ABSENT from the list.** Assert the emitted SQL text contains the outstanding-lines subquery and that the fully-returned group renders nowhere | **D21 mode A — the worklist gate is intentional** |
| **27** | **`?curp=` GET: that same fully-returned solicitud IS rendered, table B present, with a working Deshacer form.** Assert `action="/solicitudes/devoluciones/<lineaId>/deshacer"`, an `_csrf` input, both hidden filter inputs, and that the emitted SQL text does NOT contain the subquery | **D21 mode B — the reviewer's unreachable-undo scenario, closed** |
| **28** | `?codigo=` GET: same as 27 reached by tracking code instead of CURP | D21 mode B, second entry point |
| **29** | Undo POSTed from a filtered fully-returned card -> 200, the card is still rendered, the line moved back to table A, both filters preserved | full round trip of the recovery path |
| **30** | Filtered GET with zero rows -> `mensajeVacio` is the lookup copy ("No se encontró ninguna solicitud aceptada con esos datos."), not the worklist copy | D21 empty-state split |
| **31** | Unfiltered POST that returns the LAST outstanding line -> 200, success `mensaje` still rendered, that solicitud's card absent from the response | mode A is intended AND the confirmation survives the card's disappearance |

Cases 12/13/20 are the regression fences the proposal explicitly asks for — 20 in particular must read as intended behavior, e.g. `'deshacer NO revierte copias_totales — la inflación es el costo aceptado del esquema de 2 columnas'`.

Cases 26/27/31 must be read as a set: 26 and 31 assert that disappearing from the default view is *correct*, 27 asserts that disappearing is *not terminal*. Any future change that makes one pass by breaking another has reintroduced the bug this rev exists to fix, so their test names should cross-reference D21.

Cases 26/27/28/30 assert against the SQL text the mock captured, which is the only way to prove the mode switch happened at all — the mock never executes SQL, so a wrong-mode query would otherwise return whatever rows the fixture supplies and pass silently.

`package.json`'s `test` script and the identical list in `CLAUDE.md` both gain `test/devoluciones.routes.test.js`. CI runs the literal string; missing either one means the suite silently never runs.

### 12.3 Known coverage limit

The mock never parses SQL, so **no test proves any statement in §5-§7 is syntactically valid** — in particular the `(VALUES ...)` derived table, the `UPDATE ... SET ... OUTPUT ... FROM ... JOIN` clause ordering, and `OUTPUT` returning to the client. Post-rev-2 this now covers **two** list-query texts, not one: `buildDevolucionesListQuery(true)` and `buildDevolucionesListQuery(false)` must both be run by hand. CI's real `mssql` container (`db/bootstrap.js`) only serves the DAST/perf flows, which do not exercise these routes. Mitigation: run all five statements by hand against a dev database during apply, before the migration's live run. Recorded as a risk, not silently accepted.

## 13. Decisions (ADR-style)

| # | Decision | Rationale | Rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | New controller + route module, no service/repository tier | Repo is controller-over-pool; `solicitudes.controller.js` already carries a bespoke eslint override for being oversized | 3-tier split per `nodejs-backend-patterns` (would be the only one in the codebase) |
| D2 | POST answers by re-rendering the list, not PRG redirect | `renderStaffList` is the existing precedent; carries an unbounded multi-book message; no flash layer exists | query-string message (encoding/length, loses filters), session flash (new mechanism, extra write, no precedent) |
| D3 | One form per solicitud group, `solicitud_id` scoped in the WHERE | Bounds n by the 30-book cap; makes a cross-group DOM leak a no-op instead of a wrong write | one global form (unbounded n, no scoping possible) |
| D4 | Two tables per group; registrar form wraps only table A | Nested `<form>` is invalid and its failure mode is an undo button silently submitting a *registration*. Side effect that later became load-bearing: a group with zero pending lines renders table B alone, form-free, with no special casing (see D21) | single table + HTML5 `form=` attribute (valid but re-creates the hazard on the next well-meaning refactor) |
| D5 | Step 1 batched `IN`, OUTPUT is the sole authority | 1 round-trip; makes double-submit a structural no-op | per-line loop like `aceptar()` (n round-trips, no distinct messages to justify it) |
| D6 | `rowsAffected` = consistency invariant in step 1, completeness invariant in step 2 | Step 1's precondition legitimately filters rows, so `=== n` is wrong; step 2's ids are FK-backed, so `=== K` is provable | asserting `=== n` in step 1 (would fail on every legitimate re-submit) |
| D7 | Step 2 is one set-based `UPDATE ... FROM (VALUES ...)` with `INSERTED.titulo` in OUTPUT | 2 round-trips total regardless of size; book names for the message come free | per-book loop (K round-trips + a title SELECT) |
| D8 | Keep per-book delta aggregation despite `UQ_solicitud_libros_solicitud_libro` making it always 1 today | If the constraint is ever dropped, the simplified form under-restores silently — the exact bug class this feature exists to kill | `IN (...)`-only restore (silently correct today, silently wrong tomorrow) |
| D9 | Sort delta entries by ascending `libro_id` | Nested-loops plans take locks in `VALUES` order; deterministic order removes the only available deadlock cycle | relying on the optimizer's scan order |
| D10 | **No `UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK` pre-read in `registrar`** (deviates from the proposal) | `OUTPUT INSERTED.libro_id` supplies what `aceptar`'s pre-read supplied, and there is no veto to branch on; READ COMMITTED re-qualifies blocked UPDATEs. **Independently verified correct by fresh-context gate review under READ COMMITTED, RCSI and SNAPSHOT — settled, spec amended to match** | copying `ACEPTAR_CHECK_QUERY` (one more round-trip, zero extra guarantee) |
| D11 | Export `parseStrictInt` **and** `CODIGO_REGEX` from `solicitudes.controller.js` | Identical input-validation semantics; duplicating an `INT_MAX` guard invites security-relevant drift. Precedent: `CURP_REGEX` imported from `curp.controller` | copying `parseStrictInt` (proposal listed only `CODIGO_REGEX`) |
| D12 | List query filtered to `sl.estatus = 'aceptada'` in both modes | Only two buckets can exist, so the third rendering case never arises. The sibling shows all lines because approval decisions need sibling context; returns do not | mirroring `STAFF_LIST_QUERY` verbatim |
| D13 | Malformed filter -> 400, **no query**, explicit message + distinct empty-state copy | Honest: we did not search. Matches `create()`'s 400-with-message convention | unfiltered superset (contradicts the filter box and silently drops the staffer from lookup mode into worklist mode), filtered query (guaranteed-empty = the "silent empty list" the proposal forbids) |
| D14 | `mensaje` + `mensajeEsError` (red/green) plus a separate always-orange `avisoTotales`, both top-level | The raise is neither success nor error and must be able to appear alongside the success count; no Handlebars helpers exist for a tri-state class picker. Top-level placement is what lets the confirmation outlive a card that just left the worklist (D21) | one slot with a 3-way class computation; per-card message placement |
| D15 | Empty OUTPUT on registrar -> 200; empty OUTPUT on deshacer -> 409 | Registrar is bulk: a partially-already-returned selection is normal and the desired state holds. Deshacer targets exactly one line, so zero rows means the one thing asked for was impossible | uniform 409 (would make the proposal's "no error page on re-submit" criterion fail) |
| D16 | Collapse pairing via `data-devolucion-toggle` + `data-bs-target`; auto-expand only when there is a single group | id scheme stays in the view alone; per-target listeners avoid bubbling double-fires; a lookup resolving to one solicitud opens ready to act — including the fully-returned case where Deshacer is the only action | `getElementById` per instance (id scheme duplicated in JS), document-level delegation (fires N times) |
| D17 | Orange `chip-orange` + `undo` for Deshacer | Green/red/blue are taken by aceptar/rechazar/editar; orange is the guide's warning token and reads as corrective | reusing red (collides with rechazar) |
| D18 | mockPool gains `updateOutputRows`, `rowsAffected` derived from it when unset | Existing UPDATE branch returns no recordset — a hard blocker, not a nice-to-have. Derivation matches `countInsertValueTuples`; both-explicit still expresses the mismatch fixture. Verified byte-identical for all existing suites by gate review | forcing every test to state `updateRowsAffected` (a wrong pair silently trips the §6.1 guard) |
| D19 | Migration adds a loud `tableExists()` precondition, no index, exactly 2 columns | A missing junction table would make `--dry-run` report a lie and exit 0. Index is a separate reversible perf change outside the fixed 2-column surface; `devolucion_ajusto_total` was explicitly rejected by the user | blind copy of the sibling; a 3rd attribution column |
| D20 | `docs/frontend.md` and `docs/testing.md` are in scope | `CLAUDE.md` mandates a docs update in the same change for any `src/views`, `public/js`, or `test/` addition; the proposal's table lists only architecture + database | proposal's narrower docs set |
| **D21** | **The list query has two modes (§5): with no filter it keeps the "≥1 line with `fecha_devolucion IS NULL`" gate; with `curp` and/or `codigo` bound it drops that gate and returns every `estatus='aceptada'` line of every matching solicitud. Implemented as one `buildDevolucionesListQuery(hayFiltro)` builder** | **Failure caught by gate review on rev 1, where the gate was unconditional: return the last outstanding book of a solicitud and on the very next render that solicitud's card is GONE — taking its now-returned lines and their Deshacer buttons with it. Undo became reachable only by hand-crafting a POST, which breaks the proposal's own undo requirement. Dropping the gate under an exact-match filter restores reachability through the two identifiers staff already use (both are printed on the PDF receipt) while the unfiltered default keeps worklist semantics and stays bounded. A lookup by exact CURP or exact tracking code is bounded by one person's history or one solicitud, so the gate's growth argument does not apply in that mode** | **(a) keeping the gate always on — the rev-1 bug, undo unreachable; (b) dropping the gate always — the default view accumulates every completed loan forever and stops being a worklist; (c) a third "estatus=devueltas" filter value — makes the user pick the right mode to reach a screen they need precisely because something went wrong; (d) a separate `/solicitudes/devoluciones/historial` route — new route, new view, new nav entry, duplicated grouping logic, all to perform a lookup the existing filter box already performs; (e) one query with a conditional `OR` predicate — catch-all antipattern, single cached plan for both shapes, and it hides that this is a mode rather than a filter** |

## 14. Data flow

```
GET  /solicitudes/devoluciones
  requireAuth -> exposeCsrfToken -> list()
    normalizarFiltros(req.query)
      invalid -> renderDevoluciones(400, omitirConsulta) ----------------> devoluciones.hbs
      valid   -> hayFiltro = curp !== null || codigo !== null
                 buildDevolucionesListQuery(hayFiltro)
                   false -> MODE A worklist: gate ON  (>=1 linea con fecha_devolucion IS NULL)
                   true  -> MODE B lookup:   gate OFF (toda linea 'aceptada' que coincida)
                 fetchDevoluciones -> buildDevolucionesContext ----------> devoluciones.hbs
                   (modoFiltrado, soloDevueltos, mensajeVacio precomputados)

POST /solicitudes/devoluciones
  requireAuth -> csrf -> exposeCsrfToken -> registrar()
    parse solicitud_id / linea_id[] / notas      (invalid -> 400 + mensaje)
    tx.begin
      [1] UPDATE solicitud_libros ... OUTPUT INSERTED.id, INSERTED.libro_id
          consistency: rowsAffected === recordset.length
          empty -> commit -> 200 neutral
      [2] agruparDeltasPorLibro -> sort asc
          UPDATE libros ... OUTPUT DELETED/INSERTED.copias_totales, INSERTED.titulo
          completeness: rowsAffected === K
    tx.commit
    construirAvisoTotales(step2 rows)
    renderDevoluciones(200, mensaje + avisoTotales)  [pool.request(), post-commit only]
      re-read runs in the mode the hidden curp_filtro/codigo_filtro select:
        no filter + last line returned -> the acted-on card is gone, mensaje remains (by design, D21/D14)
        filter bound                   -> the card stays, now fully in table B

POST /solicitudes/devoluciones/:id/deshacer
  requireAuth -> csrfSynchronisedProtection -> exposeCsrfToken -> deshacer()
    parseStrictInt(req.params.id)            null -> 404 render('error')
    normalizarFiltros(req.body)              (hidden curp_filtro / codigo_filtro)
    await poolConnect; tx.begin()
      UPDATE solicitud_libros
        SET fecha_devolucion = NULL, notas_devolucion = NULL
        OUTPUT DELETED.libro_id
        WHERE id = @id AND estatus = 'aceptada' AND fecha_devolucion IS NOT NULL
                                         rowsAffected 0 -> rollback -> 409 + mensaje
      UPDATE libros
        SET copias_disponibles = copias_disponibles - 1
        WHERE id = @libroId AND copias_disponibles > 0
                                         rowsAffected 0 -> rollback -> 409 + mensaje
      (no statement touches copias_totales — see #148 §7 and D19/D21 notes)
    tx.commit()
    renderDevoluciones(res, 200, { filtros, mensaje: 'Devolución deshecha.' })
      [pool.request() — a different connection from tx.request(); post-commit only]
      the undo form always carries both filter fields, so this re-read is MODE B and
      the corrected solicitud is guaranteed to still be on screen
```

Both zero-row branches roll back the **whole** transaction, so the line is never left cleared while the copy count stays un-decremented. The nested `try { rollback } catch { console.error }` shape is copied verbatim from `aceptar()` so a rollback failure never masks the original error.

## 15. Integration points

| Touchpoint | Contract |
|---|---|
| `src/app.js` | `const devolucionesRoutes = require('./routes/devoluciones.routes')` + `app.use(devolucionesRoutes)` placed after `app.use(solicitudesRoutes)`. Order is readability only — path shapes cannot collide (verified in #148 §3) |
| `src/controllers/solicitudes.controller.js` | `module.exports` gains `CODIGO_REGEX` and `parseStrictInt`. Two added lines, no behavior change. No require cycle: `devoluciones -> solicitudes -> {curp, pdfSolicitud.service}` is a DAG, and the PDF service is already loaded at boot by `solicitudes.routes.js`, so this adds no startup cost |
| `src/controllers/curp.controller.js` | `CURP_REGEX` consumed as-is, no change |
| `src/middleware/csrf.js` | Its header comment enumerates "the 4 forms behind a staff session (login, libros crear/editar, solicitudes aceptar/rechazar)". Two new protected POSTs make that list wrong — update the comment in the same change or it becomes stale documentation of a security boundary |
| `src/middleware/requireAuth.js` | Unchanged; unauthenticated hits redirect to `/login` |
| `src/middleware/errorHandler.js` | Unchanged; rethrown transaction errors surface as 500, identical to `aceptar()` |
| `src/views/partials/head.hbs` | Consumed as `{{> head title="Devoluciones"}}`. No `noSidebar` (staff screen). Bootstrap 5 + SweetAlert2 + Material Symbols already load there — no per-page CDN tags |
| `src/views/partials/sidebar.hbs` | One flat `<li><a href="/solicitudes/devoluciones">` with icon `assignment_return` and `<span class="sidebar-label">Devoluciones</span>`, placed right after the existing Solicitudes entry. This adjacency is the whole justification for reusing the `/solicitudes` URL prefix (#148 §1) — the URL namespace mirrors the nav grouping |
| `src/views/partials/footer.hbs` | Consumed unchanged |
| `public/css/styles.css` | `+ .chip-orange` and `.chip-orange:hover` (mirroring the `.chip-red` block at lines 266-273, using `#f59e0b`), `+ .mensaje-exito` (`--btn-green`), `+ .mensaje-aviso` (`--btn-orange`) — both message classes shaped like the existing `.field-error` (12px, no chrome). No new class for the mode hint or the `soloDevueltos` line: both reuse `.subtitle` |
| Content-Security-Policy in `src/app.js` | No change needed. `devoluciones.js` is served from `/js/` (`'self'`), and the view uses zero inline `<script>` — matching the CSP comment's claim that `scriptSrc` needs no `'unsafe-inline'`. Inline `style="..."` attributes remain allowed |
| npm dependencies | None added |

## 16. Risks and open assumptions

| Risk | Severity | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| **No test parses SQL.** `test/helpers/mockPool.js` dispatches on a leading-verb regex only, so nothing proves the `(VALUES ...)` derived table, the `UPDATE ... SET ... OUTPUT ... FROM ... JOIN` clause ordering, or client-returning `OUTPUT` are syntactically valid. Post-rev-2 this spans **five** statements, since the list query now has two texts | **High** | Run all five statements by hand against a dev database during apply, before the migration's live run. CI's real `mssql` container (`db/bootstrap.js`) only serves the DAST/perf jobs, which never reach these routes |
| ~~Design deviates from the proposal by dropping `WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK)` in `registrar`~~ | **RESOLVED** | Fresh-context gate review independently verified D10 correct under READ COMMITTED, RCSI and SNAPSHOT. Design wins; the spec is amended to match. No action at apply time beyond not re-adding the pre-read |
| **Someone "simplifies" the two-mode query back to one** — most likely by deleting the `hayFiltro` branch as apparent dead complexity, or by making the gate a permanent `OR` predicate | **Med** | D21 carries the exact failure scenario, not just the fix. Test 27 fails the moment the gate becomes unconditional; test 26 fails the moment it is removed entirely; tests 26/27/31 cross-reference D21 in their names so the trap is visible from the test output alone |
| Mode B on a CURP with a long borrowing history returns every `aceptada` line that person ever had | Low | Bounded by one person or one solicitud, and both filters are exact equality, not `LIKE` — there is no wildcard that widens mode B. If a single CURP ever accumulates enough history to matter, that is the signal to take the deferred filtered-index lever together with pagination, not to restore the gate |
| `UQ_solicitud_libros_solicitud_libro UNIQUE (solicitud_id, libro_id)` makes the per-book delta aggregation unreachable today, so a reviewer may delete it as dead code | **Med** | Kept deliberately (D8). In-code comment naming the constraint + test 14, whose name states it is unreachable-by-constraint and why it stays. Deleting it makes a future constraint removal under-restore inventory silently |
| **`copias_totales` inflation after an undone overshoot return is permanent** | **Med — ACCEPTED BY DESIGN** | Not mitigated and not to be "fixed" during apply. Containment only: the raise is announced when it happens, naming the books, and `construirAvisoTotales` ends with "Este ajuste no se revierte al deshacer la devolución." Pinned by test 20; must be recorded in `docs/architecture.md`. Re-verified as intended by gate review |
| Losing Post/Redirect/Get: a browser refresh after a registrar re-POSTs | Low | Structurally idempotent (`AND fecha_devolucion IS NULL` + OUTPUT-driven restore). Refresh yields the neutral "ya estaban registradas" message at 200. Explicit tradeoff in D2 |
| A staffer is confused when the card they just acted on vanishes from the unfiltered list | Low | Intended (D21 mode A), and softened by three things: the green success message is top-level and survives the disappearance (D14), the orange totals notice does too, and the card is one CURP/codigo lookup away. Pinned by test 31 |
| `OUTPUT` returning rows to the client assumes no triggers on `solicitud_libros` / `libros` | Low | None exist in `db/schema.sql` or in `scripts/migrate-solicitud-multi-libro.js`. Re-verify if a trigger is ever introduced |
| `db/seed-ci.sql` inserts every `solicitud_libros` line as `'pendiente'`, so the CI container renders an empty devoluciones screen | Low | Flip at least one seeded line to `'aceptada'` (#148 §11). Confirm during apply |
| `db/schema.sql` drifts from the real schema | Med | Same-change edit adding the identical 2 columns; the file already carries its own "reconstruction, verify before trusting" banner |
| New test file omitted from `package.json` / `CLAUDE.md` (both hardcode the list verbatim) | Med | Explicit task in both files; CI runs the literal `npm test` string, so an omission means the suite silently never runs |
| `src/middleware/csrf.js`'s "4 forms" comment goes stale | Low | Same-change edit (§15) |
| Unbounded list, no pagination — in **either** mode | Low now | Matches the sibling `/solicitudes`, which has none. Mode A is bounded by outstanding loans, mode B by one person or one solicitud. Revisit together with the deferred filtered-index lever when the outstanding-loans list grows |
| Grouping logic structurally duplicated from `buildListContext` and may drift | Low | Deliberate structural (not logical) duplication — the two contexts diverge (two buckets vs. badges, plus `modoFiltrado`/`soloDevueltos`/`mensajeVacio`, which have no counterpart). Per-controller helper duplication is the established convention; the *logical* duplication that mattered (`parseStrictInt`) was eliminated instead via D11 |

## 17. Out of scope for this design

Carried straight from the proposal, restated so apply does not drift: no 4th `estatus` value and no CHECK-constraint change; no attribution column (`devolucion_ajusto_total` was explicitly rejected by the user — the migration is exactly 2 columns); no `copias_totales` reversal on undo under any condition; no return-event history or audit view; no per-book notes (one note per submission); no overdue tracking, fines, notifications or receipts; no pagination; no time limit on undo.

Also out of scope by this design's own reasoning: **no new rate limiter.** All three routes sit behind `requireAuth`, so the anonymous codigo-enumeration threat that justifies `pdfDownloadLimiter` on `GET /solicitudes/:codigo/pdf` is not reachable here. Mode B (D21) does not change this — it widens which rows an already-authenticated staffer sees for an identifier they had to know in advance, and exposes no new anonymous surface.

And explicitly NOT the fix for D21: a dedicated history route, a third filter value, or pagination. The filter box already performs the lookup; the two-mode query is the whole mechanism.

Task decomposition, sequencing, and TDD ordering belong to `sdd-tasks`, not to this document.

# Tasks: Solicitud Devoluciones

## Review Workload Forecast

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Estimated changed lines | ~1300-1700 (14 files: controller ~380, test file ~800-900, view ~180, script ~90, migration ~90, plus schema/seed/mockPool/docs) |
| 400-line budget risk | High |
| Chained PRs recommended | Yes |
| Suggested split | PR1 foundation -> PR2 tests(RED) -> PR3 implementation(GREEN) -> PR4 views+docs |
| Delivery strategy | ask-on-risk |
| Chain strategy | feature-branch-chain |

Decision needed before apply: Yes
Chained PRs recommended: Yes
Chain strategy: feature-branch-chain
400-line budget risk: High

### Suggested Work Units

| Unit | Goal | PR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Migration, schema/seed sync, mockPool, controller exports | PR1 | base=feature/tracker branch |
| 2 | Full `devoluciones.routes.test.js` (31 cases) | PR2 | base=PR1 branch; RED — suite fails, controller/routes absent |
| 3 | Controller, routes, `app.js` wiring | PR3 | base=PR2 branch; GREEN — suite passes |
| 4 | Views, client script, styles, sidebar, docs | PR4 | base=PR3 branch; feature becomes usable |

## Phase 1: Foundation
- [x] 1.1 `scripts/migrate-solicitud-devoluciones.js`: 2 idempotent `ADD COLUMN` (`fecha_devolucion DATETIME NULL`, `notas_devolucion VARCHAR(500) NULL`), `tableExists()` guard, `--dry-run` (§11, D19). No dedicated test — mirrors its untested sibling script. Gitignored (`scripts/` is repo-wide gitignored per `docs/audit.md:283`), present on disk, cannot be committed — matches established repo policy.
- [x] 1.2 `db/schema.sql`: same 2 columns on `solicitud_libros`. Committed in `341e41c`.
- [x] 1.3 `db/seed-ci.sql`: flipped 5 of 20 seeded lines (`id % 4 = 0`) to `estatus='aceptada'` (D19 risk row). Committed in `341e41c`, corrected in `4aa95c9`.
- [x] 1.4 `src/controllers/solicitudes.controller.js`: exported `CODIGO_REGEX` + `parseStrictInt` (D11), no behavior change. Committed in `341e41c`.
- [x] 1.5 `test/helpers/mockPool.js`: added `updateOutputRows` option, `updateRowsAffected` default `1`-\>`null` (D18, §12.1). Re-ran all 8 existing suites (162/162) before and after — byte-identical behavior confirmed. Committed in `341e41c`.

PR1 (Foundation) COMMITTED + gate-reviewed: `341e41c` + `4aa95c9` on `feat/solicitud-devoluciones-01-fundacion`. See apply-progress for full detail.

observations.content:
**What**: Fixed 4 judgment-day-flagged issues on feat/solicitud-devoluciones-04-vistas: (1) deduped the "Corrige los filtros para buscar." message that rendered twice (top .field-error + empty-state card) when list() hit an invalid curp/codigo filter — buildDevolucionesContext now sets mensajeVacio=null when busquedaInvalida, and devoluciones.hbs wraps the empty-state card in {{#if mensajeVacio}}; (2) restructured deshacer() to match registrar()'s pattern — both 409 early-return branches now only set a `resultado` string inside the try/catch, and all renderDevoluciones calls (which do a real DB read) moved outside the try/catch, so a post-rollback read failure can't trigger a misleading second tx.rollback()/"Rollback failed" log; (3) wired scripts/migrate-solicitud-devoluciones.js into package.json ("migrate:solicitud-devoluciones"), CLAUDE.md Commands + Documentation sections, and docs/architecture.md (new bullet + folder-structure reference); (4) fixed stale "6 formularios"/"6 forms" → "7" in src/middleware/csrf.js comment and docs/architecture.md (two occurrences in the same paragraph).
**Why**: User authorized fixing all 4 issues found by review (3 WARNING real, 1 SUGGESTION).
**Where**: src/controllers/devoluciones.controller.js, src/views/devoluciones.hbs, package.json, CLAUDE.md, docs/architecture.md, src/middleware/csrf.js. Commits a91567b (controller+view fix) and dde4ce1 (docs/package wiring) on feat/solicitud-devoluciones-04-vistas.
**Learned**: The `gga` pre-commit hook (Gentleman Guardian Angel, AI code review via claude provider) reviews the ENTIRE staged file against CLAUDE.md rules, not just the diff. This means touching any line of a file that has pre-existing convention debt (e.g. src/middleware/csrf.js and rateLimiters.js both have large pre-existing multi-line `//` rationale comment blocks that violate CLAUDE.md's "keep source files free of inline comments" rule) will get the WHOLE file flagged and the commit blocked, even for a trivial 1-word diff unrelated to that debt. Tried 3x, consistently failed with the same reasoning; the reviewer itself noted "This isn't new in this diff... worth confirming with the user whether the no-comments rule is actually enforced or aspirational before treating this as blocking." Correct move as a surgical-fix agent: do NOT strip pre-existing comments to satisfy the hook (out of scope, unauthorized refactor) and do NOT bypass with --no-verify without explicit user authorization (delegate-prompt "no bypass needed" is an expectation, not authorization). Left src/middleware/csrf.js's 6→7 fix as an uncommitted working-tree change and reported the blocker instead. package.json/CLAUDE.md/docs/architecture.md aren't matched by gga's FILE_PATTERNS (*.ts,*.tsx,*.js,*.jsx) so they commit without triggering AI review at all — useful for splitting commits to avoid unrelated full-file review noise. Also noted: scripts/ is entirely gitignored in this repo (scripts/migrate-solicitud-devoluciones.js exists on disk but never shows in git diff/status), a deliberate repo convention documented in docs/architecture.md.

observations.title: Session summary: solicitud-devoluciones full SDD cycle, archived
observations.content:
## Goal
User asked for a plan to add an admin module to register book returns from accepted loans (filter by CURP, expandable list of accepted solicitudes, mark n-of-N books returned with an optional note). User then redirected from native Plan Mode to the SDD workflow (`ejecutalo usando sdd-new`), and the session ran the full cycle through to archive.

## Instructions / preferences learned
- User explicitly redirects native Claude Code Plan Mode to SDD (`sdd-new`) for substantial features in this project — SDD is the preferred planning tool here, not the harness's built-in plan mode.
- Delivery preference for high-risk-forecast changes: chained PRs (`feature-branch-chain` strategy), matching the precedent set by the prior `solicitud-multi-libro-contacto` change.
- Execution mode: Automatic (phases run back-to-back with gatekeeper validation), but the user still wants a check-in question at each major milestone (each PR, each Judgment Day round) rather than fully silent execution — answered "sí, continuar" repeatedly rather than "run everything unattended."
- Judgment Day findings: user is willing to fix even "suspect" (single-judge, not both-judges-confirmed) findings when they're well-evidenced — don't limit fixes to only "Confirmed" status findings if the user is asked and says yes.
- `--no-verify` on the local `gga` pre-commit hook requires explicit, per-commit user authorization — a sub-agent cannot accept a relayed "user approved this" from the orchestrator; only a direct user message or the orchestrator itself running the command (which goes through the real permission channel) can actually execute it. This happened twice in this session (PR1, and a Round-3 Judgment Day fix) — both times the sub-agent correctly refused to route around the classifier, and the orchestrator running the exact same command directly succeeded.

## Discoveries
- SQL Server `CHECK` constraints are genuinely NOT one-line-additive — adding a 4th value to `solicitud_libros.estatus`'s constraint would require `DROP CONSTRAINT` + re-`ADD`, with zero DROP precedent in this repo. This confirmed the "additive nullable columns" design (`fecha_devolucion`, `notas_devolucion`) over touching the existing enum.
- The `gga` pre-commit hook (Gentleman Guardian Angel, AI-based review reading CLAUDE.md) is non-deterministic on the same file/diff — it blocked a trivial 1-word digit fix in `csrf.js` three times for a sub-agent citing a pre-existing unrelated comment block, then passed cleanly on an orchestrator-direct retry of the exact same change. Consistent with a prior session's memory note about this hook's non-determinism.
- Claude Code's own auto-mode permission classifier is a DIFFERENT enforcement layer than the git pre-commit hook — even explicit user authorization relayed through an orchestrator's message to a sub-agent isn't sufficient for the classifier to allow `--no-verify`; only the orchestrator's own direct tool call (going through the real permission prompt) succeeds.
- `test/helpers/mockPool.js`'s UPDATE-query fake dispatch only ever returned `{ rowsAffected: [...] }` with no `recordset` — a real blocker for any new controller code relying on `UPDATE ... OUTPUT` (needed by this feature's restore/undo logic). Fixed in PR1 by adding an `updateOutputRows` option.

## Accomplished
- Full SDD cycle: explore → propose (3 revisions, 5 product-decision forks resolved with user) → spec + design (gate-reviewed by a fresh-context reviewer, 2 real blocking issues found and fixed — undo-reachability for fully-returned solicitudes) → tasks (21 tasks, chained-PR forecast) → apply (4 chained PRs: foundation, RED tests, GREEN implementation, views) → Judgment Day (5 rounds of blind dual-adversarial review, 6 more real issues found and fixed) → verify (PASS, 0 CRITICAL) → archive.
- Feature delivered: `GET/POST /solicitudes/devoluciones` + `POST /solicitudes/devoluciones/:id/deshacer`, staff-only, CURP+codigo_seguimiento filters (AND-combined exact match), two-mode list query (worklist view hides fully-returned solicitudes; a CURP/codigo search shows them anyway so Undo stays reachable), partial n-of-N atomic return registration with one shared optional note, inventory self-heal on `copias_totales` overshoot (always succeeds, never blocks, with an admin-facing message), and an undo action that deliberately does NOT reverse a prior `copias_totales` increase (permanent, documented tradeoff).
- 208/208 tests passing, 0 lint errors, 15 commits across 4 local branches (`feat/solicitud-devoluciones-01-fundacion` through `-04-vistas`), tracker branch `feat/solicitud-devoluciones` not yet aggregated, nothing pushed to origin.

## Next Steps
- **Not done, explicitly deferred by the user's own standing scope**: merging the 4 chained PR branches into the tracker branch, merging the tracker into `main`/`feat/dashboard-sidebar-ux`, and pushing anything to origin. All local-only.
- Open, documented, non-blocking follow-ups: `deshacer()`'s rollback-failure path is untested; exact 30-line boundary and non-string `notas` are untested; the 5 real SQL statements have only been statically reviewed, never run against a live SQL Server instance (must happen before real deployment); `db/seed-ci.sql`'s inventory-decrement UPDATE has a theoretical (currently inert) multi-match gotcha if the fixture is ever extended.

## Relevant Files
- `src/controllers/devoluciones.controller.js`, `src/routes/devoluciones.routes.js` — new controller/routes.
- `src/views/devoluciones.hbs`, `public/js/devoluciones.js` — new view + client script.
- `scripts/migrate-solicitud-devoluciones.js` — new migration (gitignored, untracked, mirrors sibling script).
- `test/devoluciones.routes.test.js` — 46 tests, the acceptance contract for this feature.
- Engram artifacts: proposal #146, spec #147, design #148+#149, tasks #150, apply-progress #151, verify-report #154, archive-report #155.

observations.title: Fixed concurrent-loan gate gap in solicitudes
observations.content:
**What**: Widened the pre-creation gate for new `solicitudes` — a CURP is now also blocked while it has a `solicitud_libros` line that is `aceptada` with `fecha_devolucion IS NULL` (accepted but not returned), not just a `pendiente` line. Renamed `tieneSolicitudPendiente` → `tieneSolicitudOPrestamoPendiente`.
**Why**: Findings review flagged that once staff accepted or rejected a solicitud line, the CURP was free to submit a brand-new solicitud even if the accepted book was never returned — no cap on concurrent loans. Verified against actual code (SOLICITUD_PENDIENTE_CHECK_QUERY only checked `sl.estatus = 'pendiente'`, never `fecha_devolucion`) before fixing. User explicitly scoped the fix to only this gap, not the separately-flagged "comprobante doesn't reflect accept/reject decisions" gap (left untouched, out of scope).
**Where**: src/controllers/solicitudes.controller.js (query + function rename + both call sites in validarCurp/create + both user-facing messages), docs/architecture.md (2 spots describing the gate), test/solicitudes.routes.test.js (strengthened 2 existing query-shape assertions + added 2 new tests for the accepted-undelivered scenario at both entry points).
**Learned**: This suite's pool mocks match by query-text regex, not real SQL execution — so tests proving the new OR-clause can only assert the query text contains `fecha_devolucion`, they can't exercise actual DB filtering (same limitation the original pending-check tests already had). Full multi-book accept/reject line-scoping (a separate finding in the same review) was already correct and test-covered — no change needed there.

observations.title: Lowered book cap to 2 + added es_personal_juventudes field
observations.content:
**What**: Lowered `MAX_LIBROS_POR_SOLICITUD` from 30 to 2 (src/controllers/solicitudes.controller.js:19), and added a new `es_personal_juventudes` BIT column on `solicitudes` (default 0), captured via an optional unchecked-by-default checkbox on the public request form, and surfaced as a Sí/No column on the admin staff list (`/solicitudes`) next to Aceptar/Rechazar.
**Why**: User request — reduce per-request book limit and let admins see, at accept-time, whether a requester belongs to Juventudes staff.
**Where**: src/controllers/solicitudes.controller.js (HEADER_INSERT_QUERY, STAFF_LIST_QUERY, buildListContext, create(), renderLibrosStep call sites), src/views/solicitud-libros.hbs, src/views/solicitudes.hbs, public/js/solicitud-libros.js (client-side mirror of the cap + checkbox disabling once 2 are selected), scripts/migrate-solicitud-personal-juventudes.js (new, gitignored), db/schema.sql, package.json, docs/architecture.md, docs/database.md, docs/frontend.md, docs/testing.md, CLAUDE.md, test/solicitudes.routes.test.js.
**Learned**: `scripts/` is entirely gitignored in this repo — new migration scripts never show up in `git status`/diffs, only their effects (docs, package.json entry, and code that assumes the new column exists) do. `MAX_LINEAS_POR_DEVOLUCION` in devoluciones.controller.js is a separately-hardcoded 30 for the *returns* cap, not derived from the solicitud cap — deliberately left untouched. Header-level (once-per-solicitud) fields go in `buildListContext()`'s per-solicitud object literal + get `rowspan="{{../libros.length}}"` in the Handlebars table, same pattern as curp/telefono/etc. A first pass by a delegated writer agent missed: updating docs/testing.md's stale "tope de 30 libros" line, listing the new migrate script in CLAUDE.md, test coverage for the checkbox surviving a 400 validation-error re-render, and any client-side enforcement of the new lower cap (found via a review-reliability pass) — all fixed before considering this done. 250/250 tests pass, lint clean (0 errors).

observations.title: Deleted dev/CI-only files from repo on chore/remove-non-prod-files branch
observations.content:
**What**: On branch `chore/remove-non-prod-files` (commit aeee794, pushed to origin), removed `test/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `ci/`, `docs/`, `eslint.config.js`, `.jscpd.json`, `audit-ci.jsonc`, `.semgrepignore`, `.gga`, `.nvmrc`, `db/seed-ci.sql`, `db/create-database.sql`, `AUDITORIA.md`, `README.md` from the repo entirely (not just excluded from a deploy artifact).
**Why**: User asked for a list of files not needed in production, then explicitly asked to delete them and push to a new branch. I warned this would break `npm test`, GitLab CI, `npm run lint`, and CLAUDE.md's docs-sync convention, and recommended a `.dockerignore` instead — user confirmed via AskUserQuestion they wanted the full repo deletion anyway, informed choice.
**Where**: New branch `chore/remove-non-prod-files`, diverges from `feat/solicitudes-curp-codigo-filtros`. `scripts/`, `.atl/`, `.claude/`, `prompts/` were left untouched (already gitignored, never in git). `package-lock.json` and devDependencies in `package.json` also untouched.
**Learned**: The `gga` pre-commit hook is self-referential — `.gga` sets `RULES_FILE=CLAUDE.md`; deleting `.gga` itself in a commit makes the hook fall back to its default `AGENTS.md`, which doesn't exist, so it always fails. No commit ordering avoids this (the file is gone from the working tree the moment `git rm` runs). Had to use `--no-verify` with explicit user confirmation to commit the deletion of `.gga`. See also [[project_gga_hook_flaky]].

- Framework: Jasmine + Karma (`@angular-devkit/build-angular:karma` builder), Chrome launcher

- Available: ✅ (`karma-coverage` devDependency present)
- Command: `ng test --code-coverage` (not wired as a package.json script; must be invoked via `npx ng test --code-coverage` or added as a script)

| Tool         | Available | Command                                              |

observations.title: sdd-init/backend_juventudes
observations.content:
**What**: SDD initialized for backend_juventudes. Persistence mode: engram (no openspec/ directory created or present).

**Stack**
- Runtime: Node.js, Express 4.21
- ORM: Sequelize 6.37 against Microsoft SQL Server (mssql / tedious drivers)
- No migrations — tables/views must already exist in the DB; models map via `tableName`
- Package name in package.json is `back_juventudes` (project/repo folder is `backend_juventudes`)
- Key deps: jsonwebtoken (auth), bcrypt, nodemailer (AWS SES), ssh2-sftp-client/basic-ftp (SFTP/FTP), exceljs/xlsx (spreadsheets), swagger-jsdoc/swagger-ui-express/swagger-autogen (API docs), multer (uploads), dayjs/moment (dates), p-limit, crypto-js, cors

**Architecture pattern**: Route → Controller → Model. No service layer.
```
src/
├── index.js          # Express setup, route registration, DB connect
├── config/           # database.js (Sequelize+MSSQL), mailer.js (AWS SES), ftpClient.js (SFTP), swagger.js
├── routes/           # authRoutes, userRoutes, programRoutes, pagosRoutes, pagosIssegRoutes,
│                      # solicitudesRoutes, reporteGeneralRoutes, reportePagosRoutes,
│                      # reportValidationRoutes, configuracionConvocatoriasInternacionalesRoutes
├── controllers/       # business logic, queries models, returns JSON
├── models/            # authModel, escuelaModel, filesModel, pagosIssegModel, personaModel,
│                      # programModel, reportValidationModel — associations via static associate()
└── middlewares/authMiddleware.js  # verifyToken: validates JWT (Authorization: Bearer)
```
All routes registered under `/api` in index.js; `/api/pagos-isseg`, `/api/pagos`, `/api/users`, `/solicitudes` have their own prefixes.

**Auth**: JWT via `verifyToken` middleware. Payload `{ usu_id, usu_login, gpo_id }`, expiry 2h, secret `JWT_SECRET`.

**Response format**: `{ ok: true/false, message, data }` JSON shape from controllers; `ok:false` + appropriate HTTP status on errors.

**Required env vars**: DB_HOST, DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_PORT, JWT_SECRET, MAILER_AWS_*, SFTP_*.

**Swagger**: served at `/api-docs`, generated from JSDoc `@swagger` annotations in route files via `npm run swagger` → `src/config/swagger-output.json`.

**Testing**: No test runner configured. `npm test` is a stub (`echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`). No linter/formatter configured. A `pytest.ini` + `testsprite_tests/` directory exist but are unrelated to the Node app itself — they hold TestSprite-generated Python scripts that exercise the API over HTTP (external tool output, not part of the dev workflow). Full testing-capabilities detail saved separately under `sdd/backend_juventudes/testing-capabilities`.

**Existing SDD/tooling state at init time**:
- `.atl/skill-registry.md` already present and accurate/current (dated 2026-08-31); verified against `~/.claude/skills` and project `.claude/skills` — no changes needed.
- No `openspec/` directory exists (engram-only mode, correctly no openspec artifacts created).
- Project-level skills present: `.claude/skills/{find-skills, git-commit, nodejs-backend-patterns, skill-creator}`; also `.agents/skills/{find-skills, skill-creator, nodejs-backend-patterns, git-commit}`.
- MCP servers configured in `.mcp.json`: context7, engram, postman, gitlab (per project CLAUDE.md table).

**Why**: User requested SDD initialization to enable /sdd-explore and /sdd-new workflows for this backend.

**Learned**: Strict TDD marker found in session config ("Strict TDD Mode: enabled") even though no test runner exists in the repo — marker takes priority per sdd-init decision gates, so strict_tdd is recorded as enabled with the caveat that no automated test execution is currently possible; a real test runner (e.g. Jest/Vitest + supertest for Express) would need to be introduced before Strict TDD can be enforced in practice.
