observations.content:
## Exploration: Hybrid search + RAG chat (portfolio-rag-chat)

### Current State
- Fully static Next.js 16 App Router site, zero backend today: no `app/api/` directory exists at all (confirmed via glob — `app/` only has `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `globals.css`, `favicon.ico`, `page.test.tsx`).
- `next.config.ts` has NO `output: 'export'` set — the site is deployable as a normal Next.js server/serverless app, so adding a Route Handler is architecturally unblocked (not a static export that would forbid server routes).
- No `.env*` files exist yet — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and any rate-limit provider credentials would be net-new env vars, no existing convention to follow (would need `.env.example`).
- Content shape (`data/content.ts`): `SiteContent` = `meta`, `nav`, `hero{eyebrow,title,tagline,blurb,cta}`, `about{paragraphs: string[], skills: string[], education{degree,school,range,detail}}`, `experience: Job[]` (id, company, role, range, bullets[]) — 3 jobs today, `credentials: Credential[]` (kind: award|publication|certification, title, issuer, date, detail?, url?) — 5 entries, `contact{blurb,email,phone}`, `socials`, `footer`. Everything is Spanish (`<html lang="es">` in `app/layout.tsx`).
- Project data is a 3-layer merge, NOT raw content: `data/projects.ts` (curation/allow-list, always wins) + `data/github-repos.json` (committed GitHub API snapshot) merged by `lib/projects.ts`'s pure `mergeProjects()` into `Project[]` (repo, title, description, stack[], repoUrl, demoUrl, tier, order) — currently 2 featured + 3 other = 5 projects.
- Existing build-time-precompute precedent: `scripts/fetch-github.ts`, run manually via `npm run fetch:github`, writes a committed JSON artifact (`data/github-repos.json`). Its own comments are explicit: it is deliberately NEVER wired to `prebuild`/`build` because it hits a live external API and "a GitHub outage must never break a deploy." This is the direct precedent for a new `scripts/build-search-index.ts`, but the *reason* for keeping it out of the build step (external network dependency) does not necessarily apply to a search-index build if a local embedding model is used instead of an external embeddings API — see Approaches.
- Testing convention: Vitest + Testing Library, colocated `*.test.tsx`/`*.test.ts`, `passWithNoTests: true`, `@/*` alias to repo root, strict TDD (CLAUDE.md). No existing precedent anywhere in the repo for testing a Route Handler — this would be new testing territory for the project.
- `components/layout/Nav.tsx` and `app/page.tsx` mount `Nav`, `SocialSidebar`, `EmailSidebar`, `Footer` as persistent chrome OUTSIDE the `SECTION_IDS`-driven scrollable `<main>` content — this is the existing pattern a future chat widget would most naturally follow (a new persistent overlay component mounted in `app/page.tsx` alongside those, not a new entry in `SECTION_IDS`/`data/content.ts.nav`).

### Affected Areas
- `data/content.ts` — read-only source for chunking; shape does NOT need restructuring, a chunking mapper can consume it as-is.
- `lib/projects.ts` — `mergeProjects()` output (`Project[]`) is the second chunking source; not modified.
- NEW `scripts/build-search-index.ts` — build-time precompute (embeddings + FTS index), mirrors `fetch-github.ts`'s script pattern.
- NEW `app/api/chat/route.ts` (and/or a separate search-only route) — first-ever API route in this repo.
- NEW `lib/search/` (or similar) — chunk mapping, retrieval/scoring, index loading — needs its own Vitest coverage per project TDD convention.
- `package.json` — new npm script (`build:search-index` or similar) + new deps (embedding lib and/or `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and/or a search lib and/or a rate-limit client), decision on whether the new script is wired into `prebuild`.
- `app/page.tsx` / `app/layout.tsx` — a minimal mount point for a chat widget, following the existing Nav/SocialSidebar/EmailSidebar pattern (additive, not a rewrite).
- `components/layout/Nav.tsx` — OPTIONAL touch only if a "chat" affordance becomes a nav link instead of a standalone floating widget; not required by the retrieval/backend work itself. New UI surface not designed here per instructions.
- No `.env` convention exists yet — new file `.env.example` likely needed alongside `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and rate-limit provider vars if that path is chosen).

### Corpus & Chunking Proposal
Given the actual `data/content.ts` shape, natural chunk boundaries (~16-20 chunks total, confirming the corpus is tiny):
- 1 chunk: hero (tagline + blurb)
- 1-3 chunks: about (paragraphs merged as one "about me" chunk; skills list as its own chunk; education as its own chunk)
- 3 chunks: one per `experience` job (company + role + range + bullets joined)
- 5 chunks: one per `credentials` entry (kind/title/issuer/date/detail)
- 5 chunks: one per merged `Project` (title + description + stack)
- 1 chunk: contact/how-to-reach-out
Each chunk needs a stable id + source-section tag + (for projects/credentials) a URL, for citation/grounding in the generated answer. This mapping is a new pure function, does not require changing `data/content.ts`'s shape.

### Approaches

**1. Embedding generation (build-time)**
1. **Local ONNX via `@huggingface/transformers`** (successor to `@xenova/transformers`), e.g. `Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` (384-dim, explicitly multilingual incl. Spanish, ONNX-Transformers.js-compatible — confirmed via HuggingFace model card) run in a Node build script.
   - Pros: zero external API key/cost/network dependency for the precompute step; matches the "no external service" philosophy already locked in for retrieval; fully reproducible offline.
   - Cons: adds `onnxruntime-node`-backed dependency + model download/caching concerns to the build tooling (devDependency, not runtime); an English-only small model (e.g. `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) would underperform on Spanish content — must specifically pick a multilingual model.
   - Effort: Medium.
2. **External embeddings API, called ONLY at build time** (OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`, Voyage, Cohere — Anthropic itself has no embeddings endpoint).
   - Pros: simpler script, no native binaries, typically higher embedding quality.
   - Cons: needs an API key + real (if trivial) cost + a one-shot network dependency during the precompute step; content changes require network access to regenerate, unlike a fully local script.
   - Effort: Low-Medium.
   - Given the corpus is ~20 short chunks, cost/quality difference between the two is negligible in absolute terms; the meaningful difference is "zero external dependency" vs "simpler tooling."

**2. FTS + vector retrieval at request time (no external DB, given locked direction)**
1. **SQLite + FTS5 + sqlite-vec, committed as a `.db` file, loaded via `better-sqlite3` in the Route Handler.**
   - Pros: one battle-tested engine for both lexical and vector search, mature hybrid-fusion patterns documented for sqlite-vec.
   - Cons: `better-sqlite3` is a native binary — reintroduces exactly the native-dependency-on-serverless risk class the "no external DB" decision is trying to avoid; historically a known Vercel deploy friction point; forces Node.js runtime (not Edge); overkill for ~20 chunks.
   - Effort: Medium-High.
2. **Pure-JS lexical lib (FlexSearch or MiniSearch) + flat JSON of precomputed embeddings scanned with brute-force cosine similarity at request time.**
   - Pros: no native binaries (safe on any serverless/Edge runtime), artifact is a small JSON file, brute-force cosine over ~20 vectors of 384 dims is sub-millisecond — no vector index/DB needed at this corpus size (confirmed via research: brute-force is the recommended default for corpora that fit in memory; sqlite-vec/similar only pays off at much larger scale). Matches corpus size to implementation complexity.
   - Cons: hybrid fusion (merging lexical + semantic scores) is hand-rolled rather than using a mature single hybrid-search primitive.
   - Effort: Low-Medium.
3. **No library at all — hand-rolled normalized-token/substring scoring + cosine similarity.**
   - Pros: zero new lexical dependency.
   - Cons: reinvents tokenization/accent-folding/stopword handling that a real library already solves; more code, worse recall.
   - Effort: Low (in dependency count) / Medium-High (in correctness risk).

Given the corpus is a handful of CV sections + 5 projects, **Option 2 is the best fit** — a full SQLite+vector-extension stack is disproportionate for ~20 documents and reintroduces the native-binary risk the architecture is explicitly trying to avoid.

**Spanish FTS specifics**: FlexSearch ships a dedicated Spanish language preset module (`/lang/es.js`, confirmed to exist in the `nextapps-de/flexsearch` distribution — language modules are separate from the universal Latin charset presets `Charset.Default`/`Charset.Exact`/`Charset.Normalize`) providing stemmer + stopword filter + matchers, combined with one of the universal charset presets — this needs explicit configuration (import the `es` lang module), it is not automatically Spanish-aware out of the box just by installing the package. MiniSearch, by contrast, performs no stemming and applies no stopword list by default — Spanish support there would need to be hand-supplied via its `processTerm` customization hook (e.g. piping through a `snowball-stemmers`/`stopword` npm package). This is a real differentiator favoring FlexSearch if lexical quality matters, though at this corpus size (~20 short chunks) either is very likely "good enough" since semantic search carries most of the retrieval quality anyway.

**3. Build-time precompute step placement (`scripts/build-search-index.ts`)**
- Follows the `fetch-github.ts` script pattern: manual `npm run` script, commits its output artifact (index JSON + embeddings JSON) similar to `data/github-repos.json`.
- Open trade-off (per task instructions, not decided here): unlike `fetch-github.ts`, if the local-ONNX embedding approach is used, this script has NO external network dependency — so the specific reason `fetch-github.ts` stays out of `prebuild` (an external API outage must never break a deploy) does not automatically apply here. That opens two real options:
  - (a) Wire it into `prebuild`/`build` — index can never silently drift from content (`data/content.ts`/`lib/projects.ts` changes always regenerate the index), but adds ONNX model load/run time to every deploy build.
  - (b) Keep it manual + commit the artifact (mirrors `fetch-github.ts` exactly) — fast builds, but risks the index silently going stale if someone edits `data/content.ts` and forgets to re-run the script; would need a content-drift check (similar in spirit to the existing `npm run lint:content` gap-check script) to catch this.
- If an external embeddings API is chosen instead, option (a) is disqualified for the same reason `fetch-github.ts` avoids the build step — external network dependency must not gate a deploy.

**4. API route pattern & Claude integration**
- New `app/api/chat/route.ts` (streaming, chat) — Anthropic's Node SDK exposes `messages.stream()` returning an async iterable, pipeable into a `ReadableStream`/SSE response from a Next.js Route Handler; confirmed as an established pattern.
- A separate lightweight non-streaming route (or a mode flag) fits a "search-only" use case if one is wanted independent of chat.
- Model/env: `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as a Vercel env var (net-new — no `.env` convention exists in this repo yet). Model choice should favor a small/cheap Claude model given this is an unauthenticated public-facing endpoint — cost containment here is directly coupled to the rate-limiting decision below.
- System prompt grounds the model strictly in the top-K retrieved chunks, should instruct it to decline out-of-scope questions and avoid inventing claims not present in `data/content.ts`/merged project data (mirrors the project's own existing "No Invented Content" convention already enforced for project descriptions via `findContentGaps()`/`lint:content`).
- Route runtime choice (Node vs Edge) is coupled to the retrieval approach: the pure-JS FlexSearch/MiniSearch + flat-JSON option is Edge-compatible; a `better-sqlite3`-based option forces Node.js runtime.

**5. Rate limiting — explicitly flagged as an open question, not resolved here (per task instructions)**
- True in-memory (`Map` at module scope) rate limiting is UNRELIABLE on Vercel: serverless functions can run as multiple concurrent instances with no shared state, and instances are ephemeral/recycled — confirmed via research this is a well-known limitation, not a viable correctness guarantee, only a marginal per-instance circuit breaker at best.
- `@vercel/firewall` (`checkRateLimit`) is Vercel's own built-in WAF rate limiting — genuinely infra-free from the app's code perspective (no new external account/env var), BUT confirmed to be gated to Pro/Enterprise Vercel plans, not available on the Hobby/free tier. Whether this is viable depends entirely on which Vercel plan this portfolio is deployed under — unknown at this point, must be confirmed before deciding.
- Upstash Redis (or Vercel KV, which is Upstash-backed) with `@upstash/ratelimit` is the ecosystem-standard answer, HTTP-based (works from Edge/serverless without persistent connections), has a free tier — but it IS a piece of external infra (a managed Redis-compatible service + new credentials), which sits in tension with the "no external database" framing even though it's categorically different from a content/vector DB (pure ephemeral counter, no site content stored there).
- Recommendation: surface this explicitly to the user as a decision, not something the exploration/proposal phase should silently pick.

### Recommendation
- Embeddings: local ONNX via `@huggingface/transformers` with a multilingual model (e.g. `Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`), run in a build script — keeps the "no external service" principle consistent across both retrieval AND the precompute step, and cost/complexity is trivial at ~20 chunks.
- Retrieval: pure-JS FlexSearch (with its Spanish `es` language module explicitly configured) for lexical + flat JSON embeddings scanned with brute-force cosine similarity for semantic, fused with a simple weighted/RRF score combination — no SQLite/vector-extension needed at this corpus size; avoids native-binary deploy risk entirely and keeps Edge-runtime compatibility open.
- Build-time script: follow the `fetch-github.ts` precedent (manual script, committed artifact) as the default, but explicitly present the `prebuild`-wiring alternative to the user as a real option since the network-outage rationale for staying manual doesn't apply once no external API is called.
- Rate limiting: present the 3-way trade-off (unreliable in-memory / Vercel-plan-gated WAF / Upstash-as-minimal-infra) to the user as an explicit decision before `sdd-propose` locks an approach.

### Risks
- Rate limiting has no infra-free AND fully-reliable solution confirmed — this is a real open architectural question, not a solved one; must be resolved with the user before implementation.
- Public, unauthenticated Claude API endpoint is a cost/abuse surface regardless of which rate-limit backend is chosen — needs a hard cap strategy (e.g. max tokens, model choice) independent of rate limiting.
- No existing precedent in this repo for testing a Next.js Route Handler — first-of-its-kind testing pattern, adds process risk under the project's strict-TDD convention.
- Build-time-vs-committed-artifact staleness risk for the search index mirrors a known class of risk already handled for `github-repos.json` (via `lint:content`) — a similar drift-detection mechanism will likely be needed for the search index too.
- Chunk/citation grounding must stay consistent with the project's existing "No Invented Content" convention (`findContentGaps`) — the RAG system prompt needs equivalent discipline so answers never fabricate claims beyond `data/content.ts`/merged project data.
- Spanish-quality of the chosen multilingual embedding model is "good for its size" but not verified against this specific tiny corpus — worth a manual quality spot-check before committing to the approach in `sdd-propose`.

### Ready for Proposal
Yes, with one explicit decision the user should make before/at proposal time: the rate-limiting backend (in-memory vs Vercel Firewall WAF-plan-dependent vs Upstash/minimal-infra-exception). Everything else (embeddings approach, retrieval approach, chunking, build-script placement) has a clear recommendation ready to carry into `sdd-propose`.

observations.title: sdd/portfolio-rag-chat/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Hybrid Search + RAG Chat (portfolio-rag-chat)

## Intent

The shipped portfolio is fully static: a recruiter asking "¿tiene experiencia en X?" must scroll and infer. Add a grounded Spanish chat that answers directly from what the site already publishes — no new content, no invented claims. Constraints locked by the user: no external DB, no per-user rate limiting, bounded cost on a public unauthenticated endpoint.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `scripts/build-search-index.ts` — chunks `data/content.ts` + `mergeProjects()` output into ~20 docs (stable id, section tag, optional url), generates LOCAL ONNX multilingual embeddings (`Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` via `@huggingface/transformers`), writes a COMMITTED JSON artifact. Mirrors the `scripts/fetch-github.ts` + `data/github-repos.json` precedent.
- `lib/search/` — pure chunk mapper, FlexSearch with the Spanish `es` lang module (lexical), brute-force cosine over the embeddings JSON (semantic), weighted/RRF fusion. Fully unit-testable, no native binaries.
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` — first Route Handler in the repo: retrieve top-K → check/increment global cap → Claude streaming (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`), system prompt grounded strictly in retrieved chunks, declines out-of-scope questions. Mirrors the repo's existing "No Invented Content" discipline (`findContentGaps()` / `lint:content`).
- `lib/rate-limit/` — GLOBAL daily budget: ONE shared counter across all visitors (not per IP/session), daily reset, backed by Upstash Redis (default; Vercel KV is an equivalent Upstash-backed alternative). Endpoint refuses further generation until reset.
- Chat widget mount point in `app/page.tsx`, alongside Nav/SocialSidebar/EmailSidebar (persistent chrome, NOT a `SECTION_IDS` entry). Existence only — visuals/UX are a design-phase job.
- `.env.example` (net-new): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + store credentials.

### Out of Scope
- Per-user / per-IP / per-session rate limiting (explicitly rejected).
- External vector DB, Postgres/Supabase, SQLite + sqlite-vec, `better-sqlite3`.
- Server-side conversation persistence, auth, analytics.
- Redesigning shipped sections or components beyond adding the mount point. `SECTION_IDS`, `data/content.ts` shape, and `lib/projects.ts` merge logic stay unchanged.
- Admin/ops UI for the budget counter.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `content-indexing`: build-time chunking + local embedding generation into a committed artifact.
- `hybrid-retrieval`: Spanish lexical + semantic scoring and fusion over the index.
- `rag-chat-api`: grounded streaming chat endpoint over retrieved chunks.
- `chat-budget-guard`: global shared daily cap with refusal behavior.
- `chat-widget`: client surface to send queries and render streamed answers.

### Modified Capabilities
- None. No existing spec-level behavior changes.

## Approach

| Layer | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Embeddings | Local ONNX multilingual, build time, devDependency | No external service anywhere in the pipeline; ~20 chunks makes cost/quality tradeoffs negligible |
| Lexical | FlexSearch + `es` module | Only option with a real Spanish stemmer/stopword preset out of the box |
| Semantic | Brute-force cosine over flat JSON | Sub-ms at 20×384 dims; a vector index would be pure ceremony and reintroduce native-binary deploy risk |
| Generation | Claude streaming, small/cheap model, low max_tokens | Public unauthenticated surface — hard token cap is defense-in-depth beside the budget guard |
| Cost control | One shared daily counter in Upstash Redis | In-memory counters do not survive serverless instance churn; a shared HTTP-backed counter is the minimum viable correct store |
| Runtime | Pure-JS stack keeps Edge compatibility open | No native deps forced |

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/build-search-index.ts` | New | Chunk + embed + emit artifact |
| `data/search-index.json` | New | Committed index + vectors |
| `lib/search/` | New | Mapper, retrieval, fusion + Vitest |
| `lib/rate-limit/` | New | Global daily budget guard |
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | New | Retrieval + Claude streaming |
| `app/page.tsx` | Modified | Additive widget mount only |
| `package.json` | Modified | New script + deps |
| `.env.example` | New | First env convention in repo |
| `data/content.ts`, `lib/projects.ts` | Read-only | Sources, not modified |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Index silently drifts from edited content | High | Drift guard mirroring `lint:content`, or wire script into `prebuild` (open question) |
| No Route Handler test precedent under strict TDD | High | Keep retrieval/budget as pure testable modules; route stays a thin orchestrator |
| Global cap denies a real recruiter after abuse | Med | Generous cap + graceful fallback surfacing the contact email |
| Spanish quality of the small multilingual model unverified | Med | Manual spot-check against real queries before locking; lexical leg backstops recall |
| Model fabricates beyond retrieved chunks | Med | Strict grounding prompt + explicit decline instruction + citations to source sections |
| Upstash outage blocks chat | Low | Fail-closed on the endpoint, site itself is unaffected |
| ONNX model download slows CI/deploy | Low | Only if wired into `prebuild`; manual script avoids it entirely |

## Rollback Plan

All changes are additive. Revert by removing the widget mount in `app/page.tsx` and deleting `app/api/chat/route.ts`; `lib/search/`, the JSON artifact, and the script become inert dead code with zero runtime effect. The static site is unchanged and keeps building without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Full revert = revert the change's commit range.

## Dependencies

- Anthropic account + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (net-new).
- Upstash Redis (or Vercel KV) account + credentials.
- New packages: `flexsearch`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@upstash/redis`, `@huggingface/transformers` (dev).
- No `prebuild` script exists today; `tsx` is already available for scripts.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Index build produces ~20 chunks covering hero, about, skills, education, 3 jobs, 5 credentials, 5 projects, contact.
- [ ] Spanish queries about a specific job, project, or credential retrieve the correct chunk in top-3.
- [ ] Chat answers cite/stay within retrieved chunks and explicitly declines out-of-scope questions.
- [ ] Responses stream incrementally rather than blocking to completion.
- [ ] Once the global daily cap is exhausted, every visitor gets a graceful refusal and zero Claude calls are made.
- [ ] `npm test` covers chunking, fusion scoring, and budget guard as pure units.
- [ ] Site builds and deploys unchanged when the chat env vars are absent.

## Open Questions (carried forward, unresolved)

1. **Build placement**: manual `npm run build:search-index` mirroring `fetch-github.ts`, or wired into `prebuild`? The "external outage must not break deploy" reason does NOT transfer here — embeddings are local. Tradeoff is now build time vs. staleness.
2. **Shared vs separate budget**: do search-only queries (no Claude call) consume the same daily counter, or get their own cap / none? Affects whether a degraded search-only mode can survive cap exhaustion.
3. **Staleness guard**: extend `scripts/check-content.ts` with an index-freshness check, or add a separate script? Only needed if (1) resolves to manual.
4. **Deployment plan** for Vercel (affects nothing now that Firewall/WAF is out, but confirms env var setup path).

## Proposal question round (interactive mode — needs user answers)

Executor could not ask the user directly. Proposed product questions:

1. **Cap-exhausted experience**: when the daily budget is spent, should a visitor get a plain "chat unavailable, escríbeme a {email}" message, or a degraded search-only mode that still surfaces matching site sections without calling Claude? (This directly resolves open question #2.)
2. **Answer language**: always Spanish (matching the corpus and `<html lang="es">`), or mirror the visitor's language so an English-speaking recruiter gets English answers from Spanish source content?
3. **Hard declines**: are there topics the bot must never engage — salary expectations, current availability, opinions about past employers — even if a visitor asks directly?
4. **Contact data**: is the email/phone in `data/content.ts` fair game to state in an answer, or should the bot always redirect to the contact section?
5. **Success moment**: is the primary target a recruiter screening for a stack match in under a minute, or a client evaluating depth on a specific project? This shapes how the retrieval is tuned and how long answers should be.

Assumptions applied while awaiting answers: answers in Spanish; contact info may be surfaced since it is already public on the page; graceful refusal (not search-only) when the cap is hit; recruiter-screening is the primary use case.

observations.title: sdd/portfolio-rag-chat/spec
observations.content:
# Spec: Hybrid Search + RAG Chat (portfolio-rag-chat)

New capability specs (no existing behavior modified). RFC 2119 keywords apply.

## Domain: content-indexing

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| CI-1 | `scripts/build-search-index.ts` MUST chunk `data/content.ts` + `mergeProjects()` output into stable-id, section-tagged docs (~20: hero, about paragraphs, skills, education, 3 jobs, 5 credentials, 5 projects, contact), each carrying an optional source URL. |
| CI-2 | The script MUST generate each chunk's embedding locally via ONNX multilingual model (`Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`), making zero external network calls. |
| CI-3 | The script MUST write one committed JSON artifact (`data/search-index.json`) with `{id, section, text, url?, vector}` per chunk. |
| CI-4 | The index build MUST run only via a manual script (e.g. `npm run build:search-index`) and MUST NOT be wired into `prebuild`/`build`. |

#### Scenario: Chunk coverage and shape
- GIVEN current `data/content.ts` and `mergeProjects()` output
- WHEN `build-search-index.ts` runs
- THEN it emits ~20 chunks, each with a stable id, section tag, non-empty text, and a 384-dim vector

#### Scenario: Build independent of index freshness
- GIVEN the committed `data/search-index.json` already exists
- WHEN `npm run build` runs without re-running the index script
- THEN the build succeeds unchanged; no drift/staleness check gates it

## Domain: hybrid-retrieval

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| HR-1 | `lib/search/` MUST expose a pure chunk mapper, decoupled from build I/O, that is independently unit-testable. |
| HR-2 | Lexical search MUST use FlexSearch with the Spanish `es` language module against indexed chunk text. |
| HR-3 | Semantic search MUST score each chunk by brute-force cosine similarity between the query embedding and the chunk vector. |
| HR-4 | Retrieval MUST fuse lexical + semantic scores into one ranked list, returning a generous top-K (favoring depth over brevity per the technical-evaluator use case). |

#### Scenario: Spanish stemming match
- GIVEN a chunk containing "trabajo" and a query "trabajando en Angular"
- WHEN lexical search runs via the `es` module
- THEN the chunk is returned as a match despite the inflected form

#### Scenario: Semantic match without keyword overlap
- GIVEN a paraphrased query sharing no exact keywords with the target chunk
- WHEN hybrid retrieval runs
- THEN the semantically relevant chunk still ranks in the top-K via the cosine leg

#### Scenario: Empty query is handled safely
- GIVEN an empty or whitespace-only query string
- WHEN retrieval runs
- THEN it returns an empty result set without throwing

## Domain: rag-chat-api

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| RC-1 | `app/api/chat/route.ts` MUST execute retrieval, THEN budget check, THEN generation OR refusal, in that order. |
| RC-2 | Generation MUST be grounded strictly in retrieved chunk text and MUST NOT assert facts absent from `data/content.ts`/merged project data (mirrors `findContentGaps()` discipline). |
| RC-3 | The response MUST mirror the visitor's query language, translating Spanish-sourced facts as needed. |
| RC-4 | The system prompt MUST instruct explicit decline (not silent omission) for salary expectations, current availability/job-search status, and unpublished opinions about past employers. |
| RC-5 | The response MAY state contact email/phone from `data/content.ts` directly, with no redirect-only restriction. |
| RC-6 | On budget availability, the endpoint MUST stream tokens incrementally (SSE/`ReadableStream`) rather than block for full completion. |

#### Scenario: Grounded happy path
- GIVEN budget is available and retrieval returns relevant chunks
- WHEN a visitor submits a Spanish query about a specific job
- THEN the response streams incrementally and states only facts present in the retrieved chunks

#### Scenario: Declines unknown facts
- GIVEN retrieval returns no chunk mentioning a queried technology
- WHEN the visitor asks about that technology
- THEN the model states it lacks that information instead of inventing an answer

#### Scenario: Language mirroring
- GIVEN a query written in English
- WHEN the endpoint generates a response
- THEN the reply is in English despite all source chunks being Spanish

#### Scenario: Forbidden-topic decline
- GIVEN a query asking "What salary do you expect?"
- WHEN the endpoint generates a response
- THEN it explicitly declines the topic rather than answering or staying silent

#### Scenario: Contact info disclosure
- GIVEN a query asking for contact info
- WHEN the endpoint generates a response
- THEN it may state the literal email/phone from `data/content.ts` directly

## Domain: chat-budget-guard

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| BG-1 | `lib/rate-limit/` MUST maintain exactly ONE global daily counter, shared across all visitors and across search and generation — no per-user/IP counter and no split search-vs-chat budget. |
| BG-2 | The counter MUST be backed by Upstash Redis and MUST reset automatically on a fixed daily boundary. |
| BG-3 | WHEN the counter reaches its configured cap, the endpoint MUST refuse further generation gracefully and MUST NOT call the Anthropic API. |
| BG-4 | IF the Upstash store errors or is unreachable, the guard MUST fail closed (treat as exhausted) rather than fail open, and MUST NOT crash the endpoint or affect the rest of the site. |

#### Scenario: Shared counter across visitors
- GIVEN two different visitors send chat requests the same day
- WHEN both requests are processed
- THEN both increments apply to the same single counter value

#### Scenario: Daily reset
- GIVEN the counter reached cap on day N
- WHEN a request arrives on day N+1
- THEN the budget is available again without manual intervention

#### Scenario: Cap exhausted refuses cleanly
- GIVEN the daily cap has been reached
- WHEN the next visitor sends a query
- THEN the endpoint returns a graceful refusal and makes zero Claude calls

#### Scenario: Fail-closed on store outage
- GIVEN the Upstash client throws or times out
- WHEN a chat request is processed
- THEN the endpoint returns a graceful refusal and the rest of the site remains unaffected

## Domain: chat-widget

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| CW-1 | `app/page.tsx` MUST mount a chat widget entry point additively, alongside existing persistent chrome (Nav/SocialSidebar/EmailSidebar/Footer), without altering `SECTION_IDS` order or existing section components. |
| CW-2 | The site MUST build and deploy successfully when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and Upstash credentials are absent; only chat functionality degrades. |

#### Scenario: Additive mount, unchanged sections
- GIVEN the current `SECTION_IDS` order (hero, about, experience, credentials, projects, contact)
- WHEN the chat widget mount point is added to `app/page.tsx`
- THEN all existing sections still render in original order and existing tests pass unchanged

#### Scenario: Build succeeds without chat env vars
- GIVEN no chat-related env vars are set
- WHEN `npm run build` runs
- THEN the build succeeds and non-chat pages render normally

observations.title: sdd/portfolio-rag-chat/design
observations.content:
# Design: Hybrid Search + RAG Chat (portfolio-rag-chat)

## Technical Approach

Build-time script chunks `data/content.ts` + `mergeProjects()` into 18 docs, embeds them locally (ONNX), and commits `data/search-index.json` — mirroring the `fetch-github.ts` / `github-repos.json` precedent. At request time a Node-runtime Route Handler runs pure-JS retrieval, checks an atomic Upstash counter, then streams Claude over SSE. All business logic lives in pure `lib/` functions (test-first, per the `lib/projects.ts` precedent); the route is ~40 lines of wiring.

## BLOCKING FINDING — query-side embedding is not deployable

The proposal implies embedding the visitor's query at request time. That requires `@huggingface/transformers` + `onnxruntime-node` + a ~118MB multilingual model INSIDE the Vercel function — pushing it against the 250MB uncompressed limit with multi-second cold starts. **Rejected.** Also note the whole corpus is ~1,700 tokens, so retrieval here buys focus and cost control, NOT recall.

| Option | Deployable | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Embed query in Route Handler (ONNX) | No — ~250MB limit, 3-8s cold start | Rejected |
| Embed query in browser (WASM) | Yes | Rejected — 100MB+ visitor download |
| External embeddings API for query | Yes | Rejected — reintroduces the external service the proposal removed |
| **Lexical + build-time semantic neighbor graph** | Yes | **CHOSEN** |
| No retrieval, full corpus in prompt | Yes | Adopted as low-recall FALLBACK only |

**Chosen mechanism**: FlexSearch (`es` module) scores the query → top-4 seeds. Each seed propagates score to its precomputed nearest neighbours (chunk↔chunk cosine, computed at BUILD time, stored in the artifact). Fuse → top-K=8. Zero model at runtime, pure JS, fully unit-testable. Embeddings stay in the artifact for reproducibility and a future upgrade path.

## Architecture Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rejected | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime | `export const runtime = "nodejs"` | Edge | Both deps are Edge-capable in principle, but FlexSearch lang modules ship mixed CJS/UMD dist files — the exact class of thing that breaks at deploy, not dev. Zero Route Handler precedent in this repo. Claude latency dwarfs any Edge cold-start gain. |
| Fusion | Weighted sum, `0.6*lexical + 0.4*semantic`, min-max normalized | RRF | At 18 docs, ranks are noise and RRF's `1/(60+rank)` flattens everything. Both legs normalize to [0,1] cleanly, so magnitude is real signal. RRF's k is an untestable magic number. Semantic is second-order (expansion), so it must not outrank a direct lexical hit. |
| Conversation | Client-held history, resent, server-truncated to last 6 messages | Stateless single-turn | "Technical depth" was the locked use case; follow-ups are the core interaction. Server truncates and DROPS any `role:"system"` — client-supplied system messages are an injection vector. |
| Cap-exhausted | Plain `429` JSON, not a streamed refusal | Streamed refusal chunk | No Claude call is made, so there is nothing to stream. One pre-flight error path for the client. |
| Stream format | SSE (`text/event-stream`) with `sources`/`delta`/`done`/`error` events | Raw text stream; Vercel AI SDK | Three distinct payload kinds needed; raw text carries one. AI SDK = new dep + framework lock-in for one endpoint. |
| Budget reset | `EXPIREAT` next UTC midnight | `EXPIRE` on first write only | Unconditional `EXPIREAT` is idempotent and removes the orphan-key failure mode (crash between INCR and EXPIRE permanently bricks the budget). UTC over local time: deterministic, no DST library, trivially testable. |
| Env absence | `app/page.tsx` (Server Component) reads `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and conditionally mounts the widget | `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` flag | No config duplication, flag never reaches the client bundle. **Rule: NO module-scope `new Anthropic()` / `Redis.fromEnv()`** — lazy-instantiate inside the request, so `next build` succeeds with env absent. Tradeoff: toggling the var needs a redeploy. |
| Index build | Manual `npm run build:search-index`, no staleness guard | `prebuild` | User decision. |
| Widget location | `components/chat/` | `components/layout/` | `layout/` is flat single-file chrome; this is a 3-file feature with its own hook. |

## Data Flow

    BUILD (manual)
    content.ts ─┐
                ├→ buildChunks() → 18 chunks → ONNX embed (384d, L2-norm)
    mergeProjects()                                    ↓
                                       chunk↔chunk cosine → neighbors[]
                                                       ↓
                                        data/search-index.json (COMMITTED)

    REQUEST  POST /api/chat  (runtime=nodejs, dynamic)
      parseChatRequest()          invalid → 400 invalid_request
      env present?                no      → 503 chat_unavailable
      checkAndIncrementBudget() ──→ Upstash pipeline INCR + EXPIREAT (atomic)
           ├ throws                       → 503 chat_unavailable  (FAIL-CLOSED)
           └ !allowed                     → 429 budget_exhausted  [ZERO Claude calls]
      retrieve(index, query, k=8)  lexical → neighbor expansion → weighted fusion
      anthropic.messages.stream() → SSE: sources → delta* → done
                                          ↓  ChatWidget / useChatStream

## Interfaces / Contracts

```ts
// lib/search/types.ts — data/search-index.json schema
export interface SearchChunk {
  id: string;            // "hero" | "about-summary" | "about-skills" | "about-education"
                         // | "experience-{job.id}" | "credential-{slug(title)}"
                         // | "project-{repo.toLowerCase()}" | "contact"
  section: SectionId;    // reuses data/content.ts's SectionId
  title: string;
  text: string;
  anchor: string;        // "#projects" — always present, in-page nav
  url: string | null;    // credential.url | project.repoUrl, else null
}
export interface IndexedChunk extends SearchChunk {
  embedding: number[];                          // L2-normalized, 6dp, len = dimensions
  neighbors: { id: string; score: number }[];   // top-3 cosine, self excluded
}
export interface SearchIndex {
  version: 1;
  generatedAt: string;   // ISO
  model: string;         // "Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2"
  dimensions: 384;
  chunks: IndexedChunk[];
}
export function parseSearchIndex(raw: unknown): SearchIndex; // throws — mirrors parseSnapshot()
```

Embeddings are stored L2-normalized so cosine reduces to a dot product. Artifact ~65KB; imported ONLY server-side, never in the client bundle. Credential ids are derived slugs (`Credential` has no `id` field and `data/content.ts` shape is out of scope) — retitling changes the id; accepted, since citations are not persisted.

```ts
// lib/rate-limit/budget.ts
export const DEFAULT_DAILY_BUDGET = 200;                       // env CHAT_DAILY_BUDGET
export interface BudgetResult { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; resetAt: string }
// PURE (test-first):
export function budgetKey(now: Date): string;                  // "chat:budget:2026-09-08"
export function nextResetEpochSeconds(now: Date): number;      // next UTC midnight
export function evaluateBudget(count: number, limit: number, now: Date): BudgetResult;
// IMPURE SHELL — only function touching Upstash:
export async function checkAndIncrementBudget(now?: Date): Promise<BudgetResult>;
//   pipeline().incr(key).expireat(key, resetEpoch).exec()  → atomic, one round trip
//   catch → { allowed:false, remaining:0, resetAt } = FAIL-CLOSED
```

**Fail-closed concretely = zero Claude calls whenever the counter cannot be verified.** Failure cost is asymmetric by orders of magnitude: fail-open on a public unauthenticated endpoint is an unbounded Anthropic bill; fail-closed is a temporarily disabled widget. The static site is unaffected either way.

```
POST /api/chat
{ "message": string,                                  // 1..500 chars, trimmed
  "history"?: { role: "user"|"assistant", content: string }[] }  // last 6 kept, 2000 chars each,
                                                                 // role:"system" rejected

200 text/event-stream; charset=utf-8   (Cache-Control: no-store, X-Accel-Buffering: no)
  event: sources  data: {"sources":[{"id","section","title","anchor","url"}]}
  event: delta    data: {"text":"..."}
  event: done     data: {"remaining":143}
  event: error    data: {"code":"upstream_error","message":"..."}   // mid-stream only

400 {"code":"invalid_request","message":string}
429 {"code":"budget_exhausted","message":string,"resetAt":ISO}
503 {"code":"chat_unavailable","message":string}     // missing env OR Upstash down
```

Server emits stable `code`s; the widget owns user-facing copy (a refusal cannot be LLM-translated — that is exactly what is exhausted).

## System Prompt (lib/chat/prompt.ts)

Instructions in English; output language mirrors the visitor. Ordered blocks: (1) identity; (2) **grounding** — answer ONLY from `<contexto>`, otherwise say so and give the contact email (mirrors the repo's `findContentGaps()` no-invented-content discipline); (3) **mirror the visitor's language**, source is Spanish, translate silently; (4) **actively DECLINE** (not silently omit): salary/rate expectations, current availability or job-search status, opinions about Juventudes / Emerald Digital / Corvuz beyond what the context states — brief, non-defensive, redirect to email; (5) contact email and phone MAY be stated directly; (6) **prefer thorough technical answers** — explain architecture and decisions, do not pad; (7) light markdown, cite the source section by name.

Retrieved chunks go in the FIRST user turn wrapped in XML tags carrying the chunk id — data, not instruction (injection boundary; Anthropic's documented RAG shape). Policy stays in `system` so it survives multi-turn. `max_tokens: 1024` (generous per the depth decision, still a hard ceiling). Model is env-configurable (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), defaulting to the current small/fast Claude model — **confirm the exact model ID against Anthropic's model list at implementation time**. Prompt caching not engineered: the system block is ~600 tokens, below the cacheable minimum.

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/build-search-index.ts` | Create | Chunk → embed → neighbor graph → write artifact. Fails closed, leaves the committed artifact untouched on error (mirrors `fetch-github.ts`). |
| `data/search-index.json` | Create | Committed artifact, ~65KB |
| `lib/search/types.ts` (+test) | Create | Schema types + `parseSearchIndex()` |
| `lib/search/chunks.ts` (+test) | Create | `buildChunks(content, sections)` — pure |
| `lib/search/retrieve.ts` (+test) | Create | `lexicalScores`, `expandNeighbors`, `fuseScores`, `retrieve` |
| `lib/rate-limit/budget.ts` (+test) | Create | Pure key/TTL/evaluate + impure Upstash shell |
| `lib/chat/request.ts` (+test) | Create | `parseChatRequest()` |
| `lib/chat/prompt.ts` (+test) | Create | `buildSystemPrompt()`, `buildContextBlock()` |
| `lib/chat/stream.ts` (+test) | Create | `sseEncode()`, `toSseStream()` |
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` (+test) | Create | Thin orchestrator, `runtime="nodejs"` |
| `components/chat/ChatWidget.tsx` (+test) | Create | Client, open/closed, owns messages |
| `components/chat/ChatMessage.tsx` (+test) | Create | Presentational + source chips |
| `components/chat/useChatStream.ts` (+test) | Create | POST + SSE parse + state machine |
| `.env.example` | Create | First env convention in the repo |
| `app/page.tsx` | Modify | Conditional `<ChatWidget />` after the sidebars, before `<main>`. NOT a `SECTION_IDS` entry. |
| `package.json` | Modify | `build:search-index` script; deps `flexsearch`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@upstash/redis`; devDep `@huggingface/transformers` |
| `README.md` | Modify | Document the script + env vars |
| `data/content.ts`, `data/projects.ts`, `lib/projects.ts` | Unchanged | Read-only sources |

## Widget Shape

Closed: `fixed bottom-6 right-6 xl:right-24 z-50` circular accent button, `aria-label`. **`xl:right-24` is required** — plain `right-6` collides with `EmailSidebar`'s `w-16` rail at xl+. Open: panel `bottom-24 right-6 xl:right-24`, `w-[min(24rem,calc(100vw-3rem))]`, `max-h-[70vh]`, `role="dialog" aria-modal="false"`, Escape closes, focus to input on open / back to trigger on close. `aria-live="polite"` on the log, announced per completed message (not per delta). Reuses existing tokens (`accent`/`surface`/`line`/`muted`) and the `motion-safe:` convention — no new visual language. Seeds 2-3 Spanish example questions on first open.

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| Unit (strict TDD) | `buildChunks` (18 chunks, ids, anchors, urls); `parseSearchIndex` (every shape violation); `lexicalScores`/`expandNeighbors`/`fuseScores`/`retrieve` (weights, ties, empty query, k>corpus); `budgetKey`/`nextResetEpochSeconds`/`evaluateBudget` (midnight boundary, at-limit); `checkAndIncrementBudget` (allowed/exhausted/throws→fail-closed, mocked client); `parseChatRequest` (caps, truncation, `system` rejection); `buildSystemPrompt`/`buildContextBlock`; `sseEncode` | Vitest, hand-built fixtures, injected `now: Date` |
| Unit | `useChatStream` — SSE parse, delta accumulation, terminal states | mock `fetch` returning a `ReadableStream` |
| Integration | `POST` 400/429/503 paths, Anthropic mocked; **assert zero Anthropic calls when exhausted** | import `POST`, pass a `Request` |
| Smoke | `ChatWidget` trigger/open + `vitest-axe` | Testing Library (existing component precedent) |
| Contract | real `search-index.json` parses, ≥1 chunk per section | mirrors the `github-repos.json` contract test |
| Manual | Spanish + English probes, forbidden-topic probes, retrieval spot-checks | checklist in sdd-tasks |

## Migration / Rollout

No migration. Fully additive; revert = remove the widget mount and `app/api/chat/route.ts`. Deploy order: merge with env vars ABSENT (widget does not render, site unchanged) → add Vercel env vars → redeploy to enable.

## Open Questions

- [ ] **BLOCKING-GRADE**: the query-side embedding gap above changes the semantic leg from true query-vector search to build-time neighbor expansion. This is a material deviation from the proposal's implied design and needs an explicit ack.
- [ ] **Gate recommendation (flagged, not assumed)**: request a lightweight approval of ONE ASCII wireframe (closed + open) before `sdd-apply` writes the widget. Not a full palette round — it reuses existing tokens — but it is a net-new persistent UI surface on a portfolio whose point is visual craft.
- [ ] `@huggingface/transformers` as a devDependency pulls `onnxruntime-node` (~50-150MB) into EVERY Vercel build install, though the script never runs there and `--omit=dev` is impossible (Next's build needs typescript/tailwind devDeps). Measure the install-time delta during apply; escape hatch is moving the index build out of the repo's dependency graph entirely, since the artifact is committed and runtime never needs the library.
- [ ] Confirm the exact Anthropic model ID at implementation time.

observations.title: sdd/portfolio-rag-chat/tasks
observations.content:
Both design open items (build-time neighbor-graph retrieval instead of live query embedding; the widget wireframe with launcher/panel/sheet/non-modal/SSE-ordering/budget-notice/seed-questions/2-new-icons) are APPROVED — built as final below. One design open item remains genuinely unresolved (not blocking, flagged as risk): the exact `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` id. The other open item (`@huggingface/transformers` devDependency's install-time/audit cost) has been RESOLVED — escape hatch implemented, see Phase 1 task 1.6. A THIRD item surfaced during Phase 2 apply (not in the original design open-questions list): FlexSearch's installed version (0.8.212) has NO bundled Spanish "es" language pack — only de/en/fr ship in node_modules/flexsearch/dist/*/lang/. A hand-authored Spanish EncoderOptions (stopword filter + suffix stemmer) was built in its place — see Phase 2 task 2.2 and lib/search/retrieve.ts's header comment.

## Review Workload Forecast

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Estimated changed lines | ~2200-2600 (excl. generated `search-index.json`): new build script, 3 new `lib/` modules (7 files + tests), 1 Route Handler + tests, 4 widget components + hook + tests, Icon/env/page.tsx/README/package.json edits |
| 400-line budget risk | High |
| Chained PRs recommended | Yes |
| Suggested split | PR1 -> PR2 -> PR3 -> PR4 -> PR5 -> PR6 -> PR7 (PR3/PR4 CAN parallelize off PR1 — see note) |
| Delivery strategy | auto-chain (resolved) |
| Chain strategy | feature-branch-chain (resolved) |

Decision needed before apply: No — resolved. Delivery strategy: auto-chain. Chain strategy: feature-branch-chain (tracker branch `feat/portfolio-rag-chat` off `main`; PR1 `feat/portfolio-rag-chat-01-index-foundation` off the tracker; PR2 `feat/portfolio-rag-chat-02-retrieval` off PR1; only the tracker merges to `main`).
Chained PRs recommended: Yes
400-line budget risk: High (PR2 landed at ~1169 changed lines — over budget, but this matches the pre-forecasted Unit 2 split; most of the volume is test code (608 of 1029 added lines) plus a large net deletion from extracting build.ts's inline logic, not new production surface area (chunks.ts 148 + retrieve.ts 261 = 409 production lines). Not re-split per auto-chain's already-resolved single-PR-per-work-unit boundary for this unit.)

### Suggested Work Units

| Unit | Goal | Likely PR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Deps, `lib/search/types.ts`+test, index-build tooling (isolated), committed `data/search-index.json`, `.env.example` | PR 1 | Base: tracker/main. Foundation — nothing else builds without it. **DONE — see Phase 1 below, including the coordinator-directed escape-hatch follow-up.** |
| 2 | `lib/search/chunks.ts` + `retrieve.ts` (TDD) | PR 2 | Base: PR1. **DONE — see Phase 2 below.** buildChunks() extracted and tools/search-index-builder/build.ts's import updated; FlexSearch has no built-in "es" pack, hand-authored Spanish encoder built instead. |
| 3 | `lib/rate-limit/` (TDD) | PR 3 | Base: PR1 — independent of PR2, CAN land as a parallel branch off PR1 for speed, or sequenced after PR2 for a simpler single-lane chain. Ask user which. |
| 4 | `lib/chat/` (TDD) | PR 4 | Base: PR3 (or PR1 if PR3 parallelized). Independent of `lib/search`. |
| 5 | `app/api/chat/route.ts` + integration tests | PR 5 | Base: PR4. Needs all 3 `lib/` modules merged. |
| 6 | `components/chat/` + `Icon.tsx` additions | PR 6 | Base: PR5. Hook/components can be scaffolded/tested earlier against a mocked SSE stream, but final PR needs the route contract settled. |
| 7 | `app/page.tsx` mount, `.env.example` docs in README, manual checklist | PR 7 | Base: PR6. README should also briefly mention the isolated `tools/search-index-builder` sub-package (task 7.2). |

## Phase 1: Foundation — Index Script & Artifact — COMPLETE (2026-09-08)

- [x] 1.1 `package.json`: add `flexsearch`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@upstash/redis`; add `build:search-index` script — manual only, NOT wired into `prebuild`/`build` (CI-4). `@huggingface/transformers` was added as a root devDependency initially, then REMOVED per the task 1.6 escape hatch — it now lives only in `tools/search-index-builder/package.json`.
- [x] 1.2 RED->GREEN: `lib/search/types.ts` + test — `SearchChunk`/`IndexedChunk`/`SearchIndex` types, `parseSearchIndex()` fail-loudly on every shape violation (mirrors `parseSnapshot`).
- [x] 1.3 Index-build tooling: chunk `data/content.ts` + `mergeProjects()` into 18 docs via the exact id scheme (`hero`, `about-summary`, `about-skills`, `about-education`, `experience-{job.id}`x3, `credential-{slug(title)}`x5, `project-{repo.toLowerCase()}`x5, `contact`); embed locally via `Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` (q8, zero network calls, CI-2); compute top-3 chunk<->chunk cosine neighbor graph (self-excluded); write `data/search-index.json` (CI-3); fails closed. **Now lives at `tools/search-index-builder/build.ts`** (isolated sub-package, moved out of `scripts/` as part of the task 1.6 escape hatch). Since Phase 2, imports `buildChunks()` from `lib/search/chunks.ts` instead of an inline copy.
- [x] 1.4 Ran the tooling; committed `data/search-index.json` (~77KB minified). Re-ran a second time after the escape-hatch relocation — diffed byte-for-byte functionally identical (only `generatedAt` differs) — and committed the re-generated artifact.
- [x] 1.5 `.env.example`: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`, `CHAT_DAILY_BUDGET`.
- [x] 1.6 Measured `@huggingface/transformers` devDep's install-time delta (+379MB, +61s, 4 unfixable high-severity `npm audit` advisories at root) — **then IMPLEMENTED the escape hatch** per explicit coordinator instruction: moved the tool into `tools/search-index-builder/`, its own isolated package with its own `package.json`/`package-lock.json`, never touched by the root's `npm install`. Confirmed: root `npm audit --audit-level=high` went from 4 high-severity findings to **0**; root `node_modules` dropped from 939MB back to 560MB (pre-devDependency baseline); root `package.json`/`package-lock.json` have zero `huggingface` references. Root `tsc`/`lint`/`test`/`build` all still pass (root tsconfig/eslint now exclude `tools/`). See apply-progress `sdd/portfolio-rag-chat/apply-progress` for full before/after detail.

## Phase 2: `lib/search/` Retrieval (Strict TDD) — COMPLETE (2026-09-08)

- [x] 2.1 RED: tests for `buildChunks` — 18 chunks, stable ids/anchors/urls per section (HR-1), PLUS an approval test proving byte-for-byte equivalence with the already-committed `data/search-index.json`'s chunk fields. GREEN: implemented `lib/search/chunks.ts` (`buildChunks(content, sections)`, pure). `tools/search-index-builder/build.ts` updated to import it via `../../lib/search/chunks` instead of its own inline copy — verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` scoped to the isolated package's own tsconfig (clean both before and after the import swap).
- [x] 2.2 RED: tests for `lexicalScores` (HR-2), including the "trabajo" vs "trabajando" Spanish-stemming scenario. GREEN: implemented in `lib/search/retrieve.ts`. **Deviation found**: the design's "FlexSearch `es` module" phrasing assumed a built-in Spanish language pack; flexsearch@0.8.212 (actually installed) only bundles de/en/fr. Authored `SPANISH_ENCODER` (stopword filter + suffix stemmer covering gerund/participle/infinitive/adverb/plural/gender endings) in the same shape FlexSearch's own lang packs use — verified via a throwaway spike script before committing to TDD.
- [x] 2.3 RED: tests for `expandNeighbors` (HR-3), including a zero-lexical-overlap propagation scenario and a max-over-multiple-seeds case. GREEN: implemented.
- [x] 2.4 RED: tests for `fuseScores`/`retrieve` (HR-4) — weights, both-legs-beats-one-leg ranking, ties, empty query -> `[]`, `k > corpus size`, PLUS a fail-loud test for a referentially-broken index (neighbor pointing to a nonexistent chunk id). GREEN: implemented. REFACTOR: replaced a destructure-and-discard pattern with an explicit `toRetrievedChunk()` helper to clear an ESLint unused-var warning.
- [x] 2.5 Contract test: real `data/search-index.json` parses via `parseSearchIndex`, >=1 chunk per section, PLUS `retrieve("Juventudes", realIndex)` returns `experience-juventudes` as top result and surfaces `about-skills` (zero lexical overlap, real precomputed neighbor) via expansion.

## Phase 3: `lib/rate-limit/` (Strict TDD) — parallel with Phase 2

- [ ] 3.1 RED->GREEN: `budgetKey`/`nextResetEpochSeconds` — UTC-midnight boundary, injected `now: Date` (BG-2).
- [ ] 3.2 RED->GREEN: `evaluateBudget` — under/at/over limit.
- [ ] 3.3 Integration tests + implement `checkAndIncrementBudget` (impure shell, mocked Upstash pipeline): allowed / exhausted / throws->fail-closed; assert `INCR` + `EXPIREAT` fire in the SAME pipeline call (BG-1, BG-3, BG-4).

## Phase 4: `lib/chat/` (Strict TDD) — parallel with Phase 2/3

- [ ] 4.1 RED->GREEN: `parseChatRequest` — 1..500 char message, history truncated to last 6 (2000 chars each), `role:"system"` rejected as injection.
- [ ] 4.2 RED->GREEN: `buildSystemPrompt`/`buildContextBlock` — grounding-only, language-mirroring, forbidden-topic explicit decline, contact-info-permitted (RC-2..RC-5). Note: confirm exact `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` default against Anthropic's current model list (open, unresolved).
- [ ] 4.3 RED->GREEN: `sseEncode`/`toSseStream` — `sources`/`delta`/`done`/`error` event shapes.

## Phase 5: Route Handler — depends on Phase 2, 3, 4

- [ ] 5.1 `app/api/chat/route.ts`: `runtime = "nodejs"`; lazy-instantiate Anthropic/Redis clients INSIDE the request (no module-scope `new Anthropic()`/`Redis.fromEnv()`, CW-2); wire parse -> budget -> retrieve -> stream in RC-1 order.
- [ ] 5.2 Integration tests: `POST` 400/429/503 paths, Anthropic mocked; assert ZERO Anthropic calls when budget exhausted or env absent.

## Phase 6: Chat Widget UI — needs route contract (hook/components scaffoldable earlier vs. mocked SSE)

- [ ] 6.1 `components/ui/Icon.tsx`: add `"chat"` and `"send"` to the existing 6-name `IconName` union + paths (flagged modification).
- [ ] 6.2 `components/chat/useChatStream.ts` + test: POST + SSE parse + state machine, mocked `fetch`/`ReadableStream`.
- [ ] 6.3 `components/chat/ChatMessage.tsx` + test: presentational, source chips rendered BEFORE answer text (sources-chips-before-answer ordering).
- [ ] 6.4 `components/chat/ChatWidget.tsx` + test: launcher (`bottom-6 right-6 xl:right-24`) -> corner panel desktop (`w-96 h-[min(32rem,70vh)]`) / near-full-screen sheet below `md`/768px (same breakpoint as `Nav`); non-modal at every breakpoint (`aria-modal="false"`, Escape closes, focus returns to launcher); inline 429 budget-exhausted notice (not toast/modal); seeded example questions on first open. Cover all 5 wireframe states: closed / open-answering / open-first-time / budget-exhausted / mobile-sheet.
- [ ] 6.5 `vitest-axe` smoke test on `ChatWidget` open state (zero violations, mirrors Phase 5 precedent's `expectNoA11yViolations` helper).

## Phase 7: Integration & Docs

- [ ] 7.1 `app/page.tsx`: conditional `<ChatWidget />` — Server Component reads `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, mounted after sidebars/before `<main>`, NOT a `SECTION_IDS` entry (CW-1); verify existing sections still render unchanged (CW-2 build-without-env scenario).
- [ ] 7.2 `README.md`: document `build:search-index` script (now a wrapper that installs/builds `tools/search-index-builder` on first run) and new env vars.
- [ ] 7.3 Manual checklist: Spanish + English probes, forbidden-topic probes (salary/availability/employer opinions), retrieval spot-checks, `npm run build` succeeds with chat env vars absent.

## Parallelization Summary

Sequential spine: Phase 1 -> Phase 2 -> Phase 5 -> Phase 6 -> Phase 7. Phase 3 and Phase 4 have NO dependency on Phase 2's `lib/search` output and can run concurrently with Phase 2 (and with each other, though Phase 4 has no dependency on Phase 3 either — both only need Phase 1's env/type scaffolding). Phase 5 is the first hard join point (needs 2+3+4). Phase 6 can be scaffolded against a mocked SSE stream before Phase 5 lands, but its final PR should follow Phase 5 to avoid contract drift.

## Session note: two harness restarts mid-implementation
This change was built across multiple session restarts (background sub-agents got killed by harness process exits, not by their own errors — same pattern as the prior portfolio-nextjs-app change's PR6). Each time, work was recovered by checking actual git/disk state rather than trusting the last-seen agent report, verifying independently (tsc/lint/test/build), then committing:
- PR3's `checkAndIncrementBudget` (task 3.3) and PR4's `lib/chat/` were both recovered after a rate-limit interruption; PR3/PR4 were then rebased from siblings (both off PR2) into a proper sequential chain.
- PR5's route handler was recovered after a full harness restart — found uncommitted on the PR4 branch itself (no PR5 branch had been created yet). Created the branch, verified, and caught + fixed one real bug before committing: the route handler's own tests hardcoded `claude-haiku-4-5` as the default model, but Anthropic's Messages API requires the exact dated id — fixed to `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` in both the route and its test.

No external DB; global daily budget (not per-user) in Upstash Redis; simple refusal when exhausted; answer language mirrors visitor; forbidden topics (salary/availability/past-employer-opinions) actively declined; contact info may be stated directly; index build is manual, no staleness guard; primary use case is technical-depth answers; retrieval is lexical+precomputed-neighbor-graph (not live query embedding); widget wireframe approved (not yet implemented — Phase 6).

observations.title: Fixed q8 dtype for transformers.js embedding pipeline
observations.content:
**What**: `@huggingface/transformers`'s `pipeline("feature-extraction", modelId)` downloads fp32 weights by default (~410MB+ for Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2); passing `{ dtype: "q8" }` as a third arg forces the 8-bit quantized ONNX variant instead.
**Why**: scripts/build-search-index.ts needed a small, fast local embedding model for a build-time-only tool; the design doc estimated ~118MB, but the library's default silently pulls the much larger fp32 model.
**Where**: C:\proyectos\Portafolio\scripts\build-search-index.ts (embedChunks function)
**Learned**: The model weight cache lives at `node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/.cache/` (resolved relative to the package's own directory via `dirname(dirname(import.meta.url))`), not the project root — already covered by the standard `/node_modules` gitignore rule, no extra ignore entry needed. Also: `quantize`/`precision` pipeline call-options quantize the OUTPUT embedding vectors (for binary hashing), which is different from `dtype` (which controls the MODEL WEIGHTS precision) — don't confuse the two.
